articles.title: Bears honor legendary coach Mike Ditka with No. 89 helmet decal
articles.summary: The Bears will continue to honor Mike Ditka.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears continued to honor legendary head coach Mike Ditka in Week 5. Ditka, who led the Bears to a win in Super Bowl XX, died Friday. He was 86 .

In tribute to Ditka, the team unveiled a helmet decal featuring No. 89, the number Ditka wore when he was a tight end with the franchise. The Bears retired the number in 2013, and team chairman George McCaskey said it will be the last number the Bears retire.

The decal appeared on the back of the team's helmet, just under the American flag.

The Bears lost 31-7 on Sunday to the rival Green Bay Packers , a team Ditka went 15-5 against in his 11 seasons as Chicago's head coach. The teams also had a moment of silence in honor of Ditka before the game.

While Ditka is arguably more known for his stint as a head coach, he began his legend as a tight end with the Bears. He is credited with redefining the position , becoming one of the first tight ends to be used as a major receiving threat.

In his six seasons with the Bears, Ditka made five Pro Bowls and was a two-time first-team All-Pro selection. He gained 4,503 receiving yards and scored 34 touchdowns with the franchise. Ditka later played for the Philadelphia Eagles and Dallas Cowboys.

His excellence as a player got him inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame while he was still coaching.

As a coach, Ditka excelled with the Bears. In 11 seasons with the franchise, he posted a .631 winning percentage and won a Super Bowl. Following his time in Chicago, Ditka coached the New Orleans Saints, where he went 15-33 in three seasons.

His excellence as a player and coach, combined with his outspoken personality, made Ditka a popular figure in the game, even after his retirement. Because of that, multiple people and organizations paid tribute to Ditka on Friday.

The Bears added one more tribute to that list Sunday.

articles.title: 'I lost us that game': The Eagles botched a game they had to win. What happens to Nick Sirianni now?
articles.summary: For the second week in a row, the Eagles lost a game they should have won.
articles.body:
Three NFL head coaches have returned home after early-season London losses to find themselves out of a job: the 2-3 Jets' Robert Saleh in 2024, the 1-3 Dolphins' Joe Philbin in 2015, and the 0-4 Raiders' Dennis Allen in 2014.

After giving away a game Philadelphia (2-3) had won on Sunday, could Nick Sirianni be the fourth?

Philadelphia had Week 5's first game, a London date with the Jaguars, as locked down as you can be without a victory formation. Eight seconds on the clock, kicking off with a one-point lead, Jacksonville possessing neither timeouts nor offensive continuity — this was one of those 99%-chance-of-victory scenarios.

You know what happened next . Philadelphia kicked off straight into the hands of Ameer Abdullah, who charged 48 meters (53 yards, in American terms) over British turf to set up a game-winning field goal.

You can't spell failure without "if," and there were "ifs" all over the field.

If Philadelphia had just kicked the ball out of the end zone, the Jaguars would have had mere seconds to move the ball down the field and stop the clock.

If the Eagles had managed to keep Abdullah tied up and upright for one more second, the clock would have expired.

Moving back up the playsheet, if Philadelphia hadn't thrown an incomplete pass in Jags territory with 25 seconds on the clock, or if the Eagles hadn't run out of bounds with 21 seconds on the clock, Philadelphia could have run the clock down to 1 second before kicking the go-ahead field goal.

If, if, so many ifs … all leading to what will surely be a long, quiet flight home.

"I didn't make the right decision. I lost us that game," Sirianni told assembled media afterward . "No other way around it. Nothing else to say about it. I didn't do my job good enough in that situation."

One of the most damning elements of an entirely regrettable and preventable misfire is that the Jaguars did the exact same thing just a few hours before. On the opening play of the game, Philadelphia kicked off to Josh Cameron, who proceeded to scoot 82 meters (90 yards, whatever) for an opening touchdown. That play was called back because of a range of penalties , but the Jaguars learned a valuable lesson that would pay off 60 minutes of game clock later.

"We got the perfect call with the perfect kick," Abdullah said after the game . "We knew we could hit them in the alleys. That's the one Josh Cameron had one called back earlier in the game. So we knew if we got the right kick, we had an opportunity."

Unlike Philadelphia, the Jaguars didn't botch the opportunity to win the game.

So what happens now for the Eagles? This is a team that was already flailing off two straight losses coming into this week, a team wracked by an offensive line in flux, a defense unable to hold its opposition under 19 points, a coaching staff slow to adjust and unable to execute. A week that saw a significant trade (Cam Jurgens) and retirement (Lane Johnson) has Eagles fans wondering if the team has already punted on 2026 .

That's what makes Sunday's loss so devastating. They'd stymied one of the NFL's most potent offenses in the red zone. They'd allowed the Jaguars to beat themselves with penalty after boneheaded penalty. They'd managed to orchestrate a couple cheer-worthy touchdown drives — not in the second half, true, but their defense kept the Eagles in the game.

But much like last week against the Rams, the Eagles burped up a late lead in large part because their offense was virtually lifeless after halftime, with five punts and a turnover on downs before what should-have-been-the-game-winning field goal with eight seconds on the clock.

"We got to figure out our second-half offense," Sirianni said, "because we're putting together some nice first-half offense and have a lot of opportunities to put the game away, and we haven't been able to do that."

The Eagles should be 4-1, or at least 3-2, and in charge of the NFC East. Instead, they're mired with the equally underachieving Cowboys, among the injury-ridden Giants and Commanders, and unable to take control of a tepid division. And as a result, Sirianni's seat has gone from balmy to nuclear-hot.

Philadelphia hasn't fired a coach in-season since replacing Chip Kelly with Pat Shurmur with one game left in the 2015 season. Although Philadelphia has been to two Super Bowls and won one under Sirianni, that's no armor either; the Eagles sent Doug Pederson packing just three seasons after winning Super Bowl LII.

For all the trickeration, all the scheming, all the alchemy and wizardry that coaches and coordinators can cook up, football is at its heart a very simple game: contain the opposition. If you keep the other side from running free, you give yourself the time to figure out how to score. And if you give the other side room to roam, well, bad things happen — both to your team and, if you're the coach, to your job security.

articles.title: Packers Beat Bears, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Tyson Bagent, Jordan Love, Top Players
articles.summary: The Green Bay Packers took down the Chicago Bears 31-7 at Lambeau Field on Sunday, led by an impressive performance from Jordan Love, who threw for 367 yards.
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers took down the Chicago Bears 31-7 at Lambeau Field on Sunday, led by an impressive performance from Jordan Love, who threw for 367 yards.

As Chicago remained without its starting quarterback, Caleb Williams, they entered the matchup as a 7.5-point underdog, per FanDuel Sportsbook , despite having a better record than its NFC North rivals.

Williams remained sidelined Sunday with a hamstring injury suffered in Chicago's Week 2 loss to the Minnesota Vikings, but he "does have a chance to play next week," per ESPN's Ian Rapoport . Chicago will travel to face the Atlanta Falcons next Sunday.

Williams' absence proved costly Sunday as the Bears suffered their first loss since he was sidelined. Chicago managed just 246 yards of total offense, including 165 passing yards, well below Green Bay's 428 yards.

Green Bay struck first on a deep connection from Love to Christian Watson.

The Packers' defense answered on the other end, as safety Xavier McKinney intercepted Bagent to set up another touchdown early in the second quarter. Green Bay capped a 5:36 drive with a MarShawn Lloyd rushing touchdown to take a 14-0 lead.

Chicago responded with a lengthy possession in the second quarter, capped by a D'Andre Swift rushing touchdown, as the Bears cut the deficit to 14-7 heading into halftime.

Green Bay maintained its lead as Chicago's struggles continued after halftime.

Love found Watson for their second touchdown connection of the day, this time a 53-yard deep strike to the end zone.

Meanwhile, the Bears missed a 43-yard field goal, and Bagent threw his second interception of the game, once again grabbed by McKinney, leaving Chicago trailing 23-7 entering the fourth quarter.

By the fourth quarter, things had unraveled for the Bears. Bagent was replaced by Case Keenum, who threw an interception on his first drive. Both Keenum and Rome Odunze also lost fumbles in the fourth quarter.

Despite missing two field goals, from 43 and 47 yards, Green Bay added a touchdown in the fourth quarter, with Lloyd recording his second of the game as the Packers cruised to its 24-point win. .

Chicago will travel to face the Falcons next Sunday, with kickoff set for 1 p.m. ET. The Packers will host the Dallas Cowboys later that day, with an 8:20 p.m. ET kickoff.

articles.title: Texans, Cardinals' Updated Depth Charts, NFL Draft Picks After Marvin Harrison Jr. Trade
articles.summary: Marvin Harrison Jr. is on his way to the Houston Texans.
articles.body:
Marvin Harrison Jr. is on his way to the Houston Texans.

Per Tom Pelissero of The Ringer, the Arizona Cardinals traded the wide receiver to the Houston Texans along with a 2027 seventh-round pick. The Cardinals received a 2027 second-round pick and a 2027 sixth-round pick.

Mystery team revealed in blockbuster NFL trade

ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Saturday that the Cardinals were finalizing a deal to trade the former No. 4 overall pick, but it was unclear where he was being traded to.

NFL insider Jordan Schultz noted that both teams involved in the deal did not want to announce it until after their Week 5 games. The Texans handled business against the Tennessee Titans during the early slate, but the Cardinals had not concluded their matchup against the Detroit Lions before news broke of the trade.

Schefter reported on Saturday that the Texans were a team to watch, while KPRC2's Aaron Wilson pointed to the Las Vegas Raiders as a possible landing spot.

The Texans turned out to be the mystery team.

The trade comes amid a rough third season for Harrison, who has logged just five catches for 85 yards and a touchdown. The former Ohio State start hasn't had the start to his career that he hoped for, but a change of scenery could be exactly what he needs.

The deal reunites him with quarterback C.J. Stroud, with whom he played alongside for two years with the Buckeyes. That duo was electric in Columbus, and they'll look to pick up where they left off in Houston.

It is surely a tough pill to swallow for the Cardinals to give up on Harrison after using a top-five pick on him just two years ago, but it made sense to get something in return for him while they still can. Arizona is immersed in a rebuild, and the extra picks will help.

Plus, Michael Wilson has been the team's top receiver this year, coming into Sunday with 258 yards and a touchdown. Trading Harrison won't change much since he wasn't a huge part of the offense early on this season.

articles.title: Jayden Daniels Returns, Final Box Score Stats & Highlights from Commanders' Tie vs. Giants
articles.summary: Making his return from a left elbow injury, quarterback Jayden Daniels and the Washington Commanders tied the New York Giants 27-27 in Sunday's Week 5 game at Northwest Stadium in Landover, Maryland.
articles.body:
Making his return from a left elbow injury, quarterback Jayden Daniels and the Washington Commanders tied the New York Giants 27-27 in Sunday's Week 5 game at Northwest Stadium in Landover, Maryland.

Despite entering the game 1-3 compared to the Giants' 3-1 mark, the Commanders were 3.5-point favorites, according to FanDuel Sportsbook . Playing in rainy conditions, the Giants overcame a 14-point deficit to force overtime and ultimately secure the tie.

The Commanders were positioned to win the game in OT with a field goal, but after a Daniels scramble, they were unable to spike the ball before time ran out:

After modest production in the first half, there were plenty of offensive fireworks in the second half, resulting in some solid performances for fantasy football:

Daniels dislocated his non-throwing elbow during a Week 2 loss to the Dallas Cowboys, causing him to miss the Commanders' Week 3 upset of the Seattle Seahawks and Week 4 loss to the Indianapolis Colts.

The 2024 NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year missed much of last season with a similar injury, but he was able to return to action Sunday while wearing a brace on his left elbow.

On the opening drive against New York, Daniels and the Washington offense quickly worked their way down the field.

Daniels completed passes of 11 and 23 yards to tight end Chig Okonkwo, and running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt scampered 33 yards for a rushing touchdown:

Commanders kicker Drew Stevens missed the extra point, but he made a pair of field goals later in the half, while Giants kicker Dominic Zvada made one of his own, resulting in a 9-3 Washington lead at halftime.

New York made it 9-6 with another field goal early in the third quarter, only for the Commanders to answer on the next drive with a dynamic, 38-yard touchdown run by Daniels:

On the ensuing drive, Giants quarterback Jameis Winston appeared to be intercepted at the goal line, but Commanders cornerback Amik Robertson was controversially called for pass interference.

Three plays later, Winston threw a one-yard touchdown pass to tight end Isaiah Likely to make it 19-13:

The Commanders shook off what may have been a bad break by putting together an impressive, eight-play, 81-yard drive.

It culminated in Daniels' second rushing touchdown of the day, this time from 26 yards out:

With that, Daniels accomplished something that hadn't been done by an NFL quarterback in 24 years:

The Commanders added a two-point conversion from Daniels to Terry McLaurin to make it a 14-point lead:

The next drive was the fourth in a row that ended with a touchdown, as Winston hit Likely for a 17-yard score, cutting the Washington lead to 27-20:

Initially ruled a fumble recovered by the Commanders in the end zone, it was ruled after review that Likely had broken the plane of the goal line with the football.

After forcing a Washington punt, the Giants continued their offensive onslaught, tying the game 27-27 with 1:43 left in regulation on a 17-yard touchdown pass from Winston to Malik Nabers:

The game went to overtime, and Zvada missed what would have been a go-ahead, 46-yard field goal on the Giants' first possession of OT, marking his third miss of the day.

New York forced a Washington punt on the next drive, though, and the Giants made two chunk plays to get into Commanders territory, as running back Cam Skattebo had a 19-yard rush, and Winston had a 28-yard hookup with Nabers.

However, with the Giants in field goal range, Skattebo lost a fumble, giving the Commanders new life with 1:55 left in the extra session.

Daniels quickly moved the Commanders down the field with a 16-yard scramble and completions of 16 and 13 yards to McLaurin and Treylon Burks, respectively.

Just when it looked like the Commanders were about to pull off the win, clock mismanagement was their undoing.

With the tie, the Giants remain atop the NFC East at 3-1-1, 1.5 games ahead of the 2-3 Cowboys and Philadelphia Eagles.

The Commanders will have a tough challenge on their hands in Week 6 on Monday Night Football when they go on the road to face a San Francisco 49ers team that was undefeated entering Week 5.

As for the Giants, they will host the New Orleans Saints and their high-flying offense next Sunday.

articles.title: Jets rally for 17-12 win over Browns after Corey Bojorquez fumbled snap
articles.summary: Rookie edge rusher David Baliey had a breakout game with three sacks and four tackles for loss in the Jets' win.
articles.body:
Braelon Allen's 22-yard touchdown run with 3:01 remaining in the fourth quarter put the New York Jets ahead of the Cleveland Browns in an eventual 17-12 win .

Allen's rush was the longest of his career, five games into his third NFL season. The score was also the first rushing TD that Cleveland's defense has allowed this year. Allen finished with 116 yards on 24 carries.

The Jets were in position for the go-ahead score after Browns punter Corey Bojorquez fumbled a snap on a punt attempt from their 42-yard line amid rainy conditions in New Jersey. The 19-yard loss gave the Jets the ball at the Cleveland 23, putting them in field goal position following the turnover.

Bojorquez's fumble came after the Browns failed to capitalize on an opportunity to add to a two-point lead when Carson Schwesinger sacked Jets quarterback Geno Smith and caused a fumble. Adin Huntington recovered for Cleveland at the New York 48-yard line. But the Browns went three-and-out with Deshaun Watson throwing two incomplete passes, leading to the pivotal punt attempt.

Watson's 29-yard TD pass to Denzel Boston with 6:15 remaining in the fourth quarter put the Browns ahead of the New York Jets, 12-10. But Andre Szymt missed the extra-point kick, giving the Jets an opening to win with a field goal.

Throwing was tough during Sunday's rainy conditions, and Watson finished with 155 yards and one TD, completing 15-of-33 passes. Four Browns receivers each had three receptions, with Isaiah Bond getting a team-high 74 yards. Quinshon Judkins added 44 yards rushing on 14 carries.

For the Jets, Smith threw for 182 yards and a TD on 17-for-30 passing. Garrett Wilson snared seven receptions for 104 yards and a score.

Jets' David Bailey breaks out with 3 sacks

Rookie edge rusher David Bailey had a breakout performance on Sunday, looking every bit the impact player the Jets envisioned when they selected him No. 2 overall in the 2026 NFL Draft .

Bailey, 23, had three sacks among seven total tackles and four QB hits. And he nearly had a fourth on Cleveland's last play of the game, but Watson scrambled away from him on fourth-and-11 before Will McDonald IV caught him and caused a fumble at the Browns' 19.

The rookie linebacker out of Texas Tech came into Week 5 with two sacks and 17 QB pressures.

Cleveland Browns receiver KC Concepcion left Sunday's Week 5 matchup with the New York Jets in the first quarter after taking a helmet-to-helmet hit from safety Minkah Fitzpatrick.

During the Browns' second possession, on first-and-10 from the Jets' 25-yard line, quarterback Deshaun Watson looked deep down the left sideline for Concepcion, who broke past cornerback Brandon Stephens.

Concepcion appeared to make the catch at the 9-yard line, but was leveled by Fitzpatrick and stayed on the ground. However, the hit quickly drew two flags from the officials, who penalized Fitzpatrick for unnecessary roughness.

Closer angles on the play showed the rookie receiver may have been knocked out, with his eyes rolling back. His head hit the MetLife Stadium turf, causing his neck to bend forward awkwardly.

Concepcion was on the turf for several minutes before being helped to his feet by Browns trainers. He immediately went to the locker room for evaluation and was soon ruled out for the remainder of the game.

Following the game, Browns coach Todd Monken called the collision " a bang-bang play ," and said he didn't think Fitzpatrick was a dirty player.

Coming into Week 5, Concepcion was tied for the team lead with 17 receptions and was second with 144 yards. He left Sunday's game with one catch for five receiving yards.

articles.title: Dan Quinn Slams Headseat on Video as Jayden Daniels, Commanders Trolled by Fans for Tie vs. Giants
articles.summary: The Washington Commanders gave the rest of the NFL a lesson in clock mismanagement in overtime against the New York Giants on Sunday.
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders gave the rest of the NFL a lesson in clock mismanagement in overtime against the New York Giants on Sunday.

Following a costly Cam Skattebo fumble, the game was tied with just seconds remaining when quarterback Jayden Daniels took a sack. With no timeouts remaining, the Commanders had to scramble to the line of scrimmage to spike the ball and set up a field goal, but they couldn't get a play off, and the game ended in a tie.

Fans blasted Daniels, Dan Quinn and the Commanders for the late-game error on social media.

The Commanders' woes began well before overtime. After allowing the Giants to make a second-half comeback, Daniels and the offense had one last chance to score in regulation, but instead had to punt, setting up overtime.

The Giants got the ball first in overtime and missed a field goal, but Washington faced a three-and-out on its first overtime drive.

The Commanders' defense stepped up to force Skattebo to fumble in the red zone, leaving just under two minutes to make a field goal or score. A string of passes and runs got the ball where it needed to be, but the lack of time management led to a play that will be remembered by Commanders fans for the rest of the year.

Washington hoped to get back on track with a win with Daniels back under center, but it will instead move to 1-3-1 as the playoffs continue to fall further out of reach.

The good news for the Commanders is that the NFC East has collectively struggled to start the year, so winning the division to reach the postseason is still realistic.

Things will get even more difficult next week, though, as Washington takes on an undefeated San Francisco 49ers squad.

articles.title: Packers' Zaire Franklin Says Luther Burden 'Quit,' Blasts Bears WR for Comments Before Rivalry Game
articles.summary: Green Bay Packers linebacker Zaire Franklin had some strong words for Chicago Bears wide receiver Luther Burden III following the Packers' 31-7 home win on Sunday.
articles.body:
Green Bay Packers linebacker Zaire Franklin had some strong words for Chicago Bears wide receiver Luther Burden III following the Packers' 31-7 home win on Sunday.

Speaking to reporters after the game, Franklin said Burden has never done anything in the NFL and added, "He quit today. He didn't wanna play no more."

Franklin's comments were in reference to something Burden said in the days leading up to the game.

Last Monday, Burden discussed head coach Ben Johnson's message to the team ahead of a huge NFC North rivalry game against the Packers, telling reporters , "He wants to beat them really bad like everyone else in the room, like every Chicago fan. Beat them real bad, and make them quit."

Playing without starting quarterback Caleb Williams for a third straight game due to injury, the Bears couldn't get much of anything going offensively Sunday, as the Packers held them to 246 total yards.

With backups Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum both seeing some action in the game, Burden led the Bears with just four receptions for 47 yards.

Meanwhile, Franklin spearheaded the Packers' defensive attack, registering nine tackles, one tackle for loss and one pass defended.

The Green Bay defense forced four turnovers, all of which were interceptions by Bagent and Keenum.

It was a massive win for the Packers, as it brought their record to 3-2, which is the same mark as the Bears.

Both teams trail the 5-0 Minnesota Vikings by two games for the NFC North lead.

articles.title: Texans trade for WR Marvin Harrison Jr., head coach Demeco Ryans confirms to reporters
articles.summary: After initial speculation, head coach Demeco Ryans announced that the team had acquired Harrison following Sunday's win over the Titans.
articles.body:
The Arizona Cardinals have reportedly finalized a deal to trade 2024 No. 4 overall draft pick Marvin Harrison Jr. to the Houston Texans, NFL insiders Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter reported.

The Cardinals will send Harrison and a seventh-round pick to the Texans in exchange for a 2027 second-round and sixth-round pick, per reports.

Head coach Demeco Ryans confirmed the news to reporters following Sunday's Week 5 win over the Tennessee Titans .

Word of a potential deal came Saturday, though the destination was unknown and reports indicated the trade wouldn't be completed until after Sunday's games were played. Harrison was inactive Sunday for the Cardinals' home game against the Detroit Lions .

The trade reunites Harrison with quarterback C.J. Stroud, with whom he'd established an impeccable rapport at Ohio State, where Stroud developed into a two-time Heisman Trophy finalist and the 2023 No. 2 overall draft pick.

Harrison now joins a Texans wide receiver room headlined by star Nico Collins, a group that has struggled to find its No. 2 receiver following a season-ending ACL injury to 2025 second-round pick Jayden Higgins in training camp this season.

Houston acquired Kayshon Boutte from the New England Patriots before the season in an effort to fill that WR2 void, sending safety Jaylen Reed and a draft pick in the swap . Boutte's impact has been minimal, however, with 12 catches for 153 receiving yards over five games.

Rumors of a potential trade heated up in recent weeks following Harrison's slow start to the 2026 campaign. A former Heisman finalist, Harrison has amassed a meager 5-85-1 stat line this season and is averaging just 21.3 receiving yards per game with a career-low 38.5% catch rate.

While Harrison has struggled to live up to his billing in his professional career, another Cardinals wide receiver has found his stride. Michael Wilson, a 2023 third-rounder, had a breakout campaign last season, with 78 catches for 1,006 receiving yards and seven touchdowns, second on the team to All-Pro tight end Trey McBride. Wilson was rewarded with a three-year, $75 million contract extension this offseason.

Wilson currently leads a 1-3 Arizona team with 258 receiving yards. Harrison, meanwhile, had been targeted a head-scratching 13 times through the first four weeks of the season, according to Pro Football Reference . Harrison clocked out with one reception in the season opener and last week's loss to the New York Giants, although he scored his lone touchdown in that game. He finished with zero catches in a Week 2 blowout loss to the Seattle Seahawks. His most success under first-year head coach Mike LaFleur was in Week 3, when he reeled in three passes for 40 yards in a setback against the San Francisco 49ers.

The thought was that perhaps a change in offensive scheme could maximize the skill set of the 6-foot-3, 220-pound Harrison. After all, he hardly enjoyed consistent production under former Cardinals offensive coordinator Drew Petzing, who's now in his first season as the Lions' OC. At one point, Marvin Harrison Sr. even aired his frustration about Arizona's offense .

With Petzing calling the shots, Harrison Jr.'s limited involvement was a frequent talking point during his first two seasons in the league. So was the on-field connection between then-quarterback Kyler Murray and Harrison, a dynamic that stuttered and flummoxed occasionally. Not coming back to the ball at times or not high-pointing it at others didn't help Harrison's cause. Untimely drops also haunted him, most notably one that turned into a Seahawks interception during Arizona's early-season "Thursday Night Football" defeat last year.

But even with Murray and Petzing gone, Harrison hasn't taken off in the desert. Actually, his role has shriveled up.

Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett is clearly in lockstep with Wilson, and McBride has accrued a team-high 46 targets through four games, whereas Harrison has often appeared to be an afterthought in the LaFleur offense.

Harrison told reporters this week that he wasn't paying attention to the trade speculation.

Yet it's important to point out that Harrison hired a pair of agents on Sept. 23 — he previously didn't have an agent — three days after he went without a catch against the Seahawks, according to ESPN , which cited the NFLPA online database.

Harrison reportedly hired that representation to navigate a possible trade. While the Cardinals already paid Harrison his $22.5 million signing bonus, per ESPN, whichever team acquired him would have to decide on his fifth-year option this coming offseason.

Despite Harrison's underwhelming numbers in Arizona, he isn't far removed from a remarkable college career. Plus, he's teased his tantalizing talent with the Cardinals. As a rookie in 2024, he caught 62 passes for 885 yards and eight touchdowns. His sophomore campaign was adversely affected by injuries, but he mounted 608 receiving yards and four scores across 12 games in a season he ended on IR .

A change of scenery could be what Harrison needs to realize his potential, or at least play a bigger role in Year 3 of his NFL career.

articles.title: Ben Johnson Says Bears Got 'Punched in the Face' by Packers in Blowout Loss
articles.summary: The Green Bay Packers smacked their NFC North rivals around on Sunday, beating the Chicago Bears 31-7 while putting up 428 yards of total offense and holding the vaunted Chicago ground game to just 81 rushing yards.
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers smacked their NFC North rivals around on Sunday, beating the Chicago Bears 31-7 while putting up 428 yards of total offense and holding the vaunted Chicago ground game to just 81 rushing yards.

"We got punched in the face," Bears' head coach Ben Johnson told reporters after the loss.

Last week, Chicago's offense was so dominant—rushing for 232 yards and holding the ball for over 42 minutes—that the New York Jets only ran 32 plays on offense.

Linebacker Devin Bush said it was a pretty boring affair.

"Holding the ball for 42 minutes is kinda wild," he told reporters last week. "Probably one of the easiest NFL games I done played in and I'm not sore at all. Great. ... Yeah, it was boring. I got bored a couple of times, I had to stay warm just in case."

Bush was surely a bit more engaged on Sunday, however. Green Bay's Jordan Love was fantastic in the win, finishing 25-of-31 for 367 yards and two touchdowns, while Chicago's Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum combined to throw three interceptions and no touchdowns.

It was a rough week for Chicago, which dropped to 3-2 after the loss, though Johnson is keeping the faith.

"I believe in this coaching staff, I believe in our players and I believe in our process," he told reporters . "So, the process doesn't change. The process doesn't change. It's Week 5. I know we'll respond the right way. We got the right guys in this building."

Up next for the Bears is a matchup against the Atlanta Falcons on Oct. 18.

articles.title: Grade the trade: Marvin Harrison Jr. goes to the Houston Texans
articles.summary: No team topped Houston's offer for Marvin Harrison Jr.
articles.body:
Nobody outbid the Houston Texans for receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. Whether that's a win for the Texans remains to be seen.

The Texans landed Harrison, the disappointing receiver from the Arizona Cardinals. It was reported Saturday that the Cardinals were finalizing details on a trade for Harrison, but no team was announced. No team made a better offer to the Cardinals at the last minute, so Harrison and a 2027 seventh-round pick go to Houston for a 2027 second-round drft pick and a 2027 sixth-round pick, according to multiple reports including ESPN .

It gives Harrison a second chance. And Arizona recoups some value after a draft whiff on Harrison.

The Cardinals didn't get a first-round draft pick for Harrison. That was unrealistic. Harrison hasn't played well enough to get that kind of return.

It's surprising they got a second-rounder for Harrison considering how he has looked in the NFL. In 33 games, Harrison had 1,578 yards and 13 touchdowns. That's not terrible but also nowhere near what was expected from him when the Cardinals made him the fourth pick in a stacked 2024 NFL Draft.

A new regime clearly was done with Harrison. It prioritized Michael Wilson as the No. 1 receiver. Harrison had one catch through the first two games of the season. His routes lacked any explosion or separation , either because he was disinterested or his athleticism coming into the NFL was overrated. Either way, the Cardinals decided quickly into the season they were done with him.

It's a miserable draft miss by a team that has missed a lot of high picks. There should be some credit for getting a second-round pick and late-round pick swap back from a Houston team that is 1-4 and could have a high pick. But it's hard to be too excited for a team that threw in the towel on the fourth overall pick after 33 unproductive games.

It's also hard to be that excited for a team getting Harrison, who has done very little in his NFL career.

Harrison's production isn't even worthy of a second-round pick, at least to this point. He averaged 47.8 yards per game with the Cardinals and had plenty of duds. He has two 100-yard games in two-plus seasons. Michael Wilson looked way better in the offense.

The Texans paid up for Harrison's prospect pedigree, plain and simple.

That could work out. Harrison was considered an elite prospect. Houston must believe that it can get more out of Harrison than what Arizona did. If the Texans can get Harrison back to his college level, the trade will be a big win for them. We'll see.

The Texans also need receiver depth. Nico Collins doesn't have much behind him, and Collins has missed a lot of time with injuries. Houston doesn't think its season is done at 1-4, and Harrison is also a play for the future.

Houston believes in Harrison, and maybe that's fair. It's hard to judge any player after 33 games. But his NFL tape hasn't been impressive and if all the Texans are getting is the same version of Harrison that we saw in Arizona, it is not worth a second-round pick.

At this point, it's blind faith that we'll see the Harrison that starred at Ohio State. And it's not like he was cheap for Houston.

articles.title: Everything Jayden Daniels Said About Commanders' Clock Management at End of Tie vs. Giants
articles.summary: The Washington Commanders blew a chance for a game-winning field goal on Sunday during a 27-27 tie against the New York Giants, failing to spike the ball in time after running a haphazard final play.
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders blew a chance for a game-winning field goal on Sunday during a 27-27 tie against the New York Giants, failing to spike the ball in time after running a haphazard final play.

"We've just got to communicate that, that's the whole thing," quarterback Jayden Daniels told reporters when asked if he knew the Commanders were out of timeous before the final play. "It starts with me, communicating to the whole offense in the huddle. And I think everybody will say that from the top down."

Washington head coach Dan Quinn also took the blame.

"That last sequence... throw it out of bounds, clock it, give yourself a chance to kick," he told reporters. "We pride ourselves on those moments at the end of games. And after the first-down run, still trying to gain more for the kick, and the right call honestly is that we can go clock it early. Don't put ourselves in that spot. And that's my responsibility, nobody else's."

Whoever was ultimately at fault, both Daniels and Quinn were heavily criticized for that sequence after the game:

The tie dropped Washington to 1-3-1 on the season, and just as importantly blew an opportunity to make up ground on the Giants, who remarkably sit atop the division at 3-1-1 (both the Philadelphia Eagles and Dallas Cowboys are 2-3).

Somehow all four NFC East teams failed to win in Week 5 despite two of them playing each other. You don't see that happen very often.

articles.title: Raiders QB Fernando Mendoza makes solid NFL debut in garbage time against Patriots, but Kirk Cousins' starting job is safe for now
articles.summary: With Sunday's game long lost, the Raiders decided to get their first real NFL look at rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza.
articles.body:
With Sunday's game long lost, the Las Vegas Raiders decided to get their first real NFL look at rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza.

The No. 1 overall pick out of Indiana took over to lead the Raiders' offense on their final drive of Sunday's 45-17 loss to the New England Patriots . He was able to move the ball on a low-stakes possession that ultimately fell short of producing points.

His first NFL snap produced a handoff for a 3-yard gain from the Las Vegas 35-yard line. But head coach Klint Kubiak and offensive coordinator Andrew Janocko gave him a chance to show his stuff against a real, live NFL defense from there.

Mendoza's first NFL pass was a check down to running back Dylan Laube, followed by a third-down pass past the sticks to tight end Ian Thomas for a first down.

His next pass was perhaps his best. Mendoza went through his progressions as the Patriots dropped seven in coverage and found receiver Tre Tucker in a soft spot in New England's zone for a 16-yard gain on first-and-10 from midfield.

He ultimately completed his first five NFL passes to move the Raiders into the red zone. He escaped pressure on his fifth pass to successfully find Laube again for a first down to the New England 20.

On fourth-and-5 at the New England 14, there was no need to kick a meaningless field goal. The Raiders went for it.

The Patriots brought pressure with an eight-man blitz, and Mendoza found himself under duress. He scrambled to his right and was tackled just short of the line to gain, and his first NFL drive ended with a turnover on downs.

Mendoza finished his first NFL drive completing 6-of-8 passes for 48 yards. The possession didn't produce a score, but he looked poised and in command of an NFL offense that drove down the field against a Patriots defense that was playing to avoid allowing the big play.

When will Mendoza take over Raiders offense?

After the game, head coach Klint Kubiak verified what was suspected in his decision to bring Mendoza in late for starter Kirk Cousins. Cousins' job, for now, is not at risk. He's still QB 1 .

"I wanted to get him some exposure," Kubiak told reporters of playing Mendoza.

"He did a good job," Kubiak said , per the Las Vegas Review Journal. "Yeah, he did a good job. All reps are valuable. Very important for him."

Mendoza's status for 2026 was one of the biggest questions entering the NFL season. Kubiak made clear from the start of training camp that Cousins was the starter and there would be no competition for the job.

But Mendoza's status as the team's starter is a matter of when, not if, leading to speculation over when he'd get his chance to take over. A 3-0 start under Cousins suggested that he might learn from the bench his entire rookie season.

Two straight losses haven't threatened Cousins' status as the starter for now. But if they start to pile up, the calls to play Mendoza will surely start to grow.

images.caption: Fernando Mendoza looked poised in his first regular-season action against an NFL defense. (Edward Monigan IV via Getty Images)

articles.title: 49ers LB Dre Greenlaw ejected vs. Seahawks for head-butt of Ernest Jones IV during sideline scuffle
articles.summary: Greenlaw took the bait from Ernest Jones IV, leading to his ejection from a critical NFC West clash.
articles.body:
There's little love lost between the NFC West rival Seattle Seahawks and San Francisco 49ers.

Take, for instance, Sunday's high-stakes game that produced a sideline scuffle and an ejection in the first half.

With Seattle driving in the second quarter, quarterback Sam Darnold scrambled near midfield on second-and-6. Greenlaw hit Darnold as Darnold stepped out of bounds, and the Seattle quarterback went tumbling into the Seahawks sideline.

Darnold's teammates immediately surrounded Greenlaw, and jawing ensued.

Amid the ruckus, Greenlaw and Seahawks linebacker Ernest Jones IV went toe-to-toe. Jones appeared to bait Greenlaw by getting in his face. Greenlaw took the bait, delivering a head butt to Jones.

Greenlaw was wearing a helmet. Jones was not.

This led to the disqualification of Greenlaw, who was also flagged for a late hit on Darnold.

The Seahawks went on to score a field goal on the drive, and the 49ers were left to play the remainder of the critical division game without a starting linebacker.

This isn't the first time Greenlaw's lost his cool on the field.

He was ejected in 2023 from a 49ers game against the Philadelphia Eagles for a confrontation involving Eagles receiver DeVonta Smith and Eagles security chief "Big Dom" DiSandro .

Just last week, he yelled at and taunted Broncos head coach Sean Payton following San Francisco's win over Denver.

During the game, he taunted the Denver sidelined and exchanged words with Payton after he made a tackle.

articles.title: Grading Marvin Harrison Jr. Blockbuster NFL Trade Between Cardinals and Texans
articles.summary: We don't often see blockbuster NFL trades transpire right in the middle of a regular-season Sunday. However, that's exactly what we saw in Week 5, though it didn't exactly come as a surprise.
articles.body:
We don't often see blockbuster NFL trades transpire right in the middle of a regular-season Sunday. However, that's exactly what we saw in Week 5, though it didn't exactly come as a surprise.

On Saturday, ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported that the Arizona Cardinals were working to finalize a trade involving wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. While details were scarce on Saturday, aside from the fact that Harrison would be inactive on Sunday, it was clear that the receiver's time in Arizona was over.

On Sunday afternoon, Schefter and Rapoport reported that the Houston Texans are acquiring Harrison in exchange for 2027 second- and sixth-round draft picks.

The deal brings an end to the disappointing first chapter of a player who was largely viewed as a "can't-miss" prospect in 2024. It also means a fresh start for all parties involved.

Let's take a closer look at the deal, Harrison, and what the trade means for the receiver, the Texans, and the Cardinals.

After drafting Harrison fourth overall in 2024, Cardinals general manager Monti Ossenfort would certainly wish he wasn't trading the Ohio State product less than three years later. All things considered, however, Ossenfort and the Cardinals did well to get the return that they did.

Harrison did flash a ton of potential during his rookie campaign, which he finished with 885 yards and eight touchdowns. However, the former Buckeyes star hasn't looked or performed like the same receiver since he decided to bulk up ahead of his sophomore season.

The 2023 Fred Biletnikoff Award winner certainly didn't look like the same big-play threat he was in college.

In his second season, Harrison failed to separate as easily as he did in Year 1, and fellow wideout Michael Wilson emerged as a much more dependable No. 1 perimeter target. While Wilson finished that season with 1,006 yards and seven touchdowns, Harrison had just 68 yards and four scores.

Wilson got a three-year, $75 million extension in the offseason, which immediately brought Harrison's long-term future into question. Arizona now had a lot invested in Wilson and star tight end Trey McBride, and it had just used a high first-round pick on running back Jeremiyah Love .

Barring a Year 3 breakout, it would be impossible to justify extending Harrison when he became eligible in 2027. And instead of breaking out, Harrison sank further into obscurity in Mike LaFlaur's offense.

Through the first month of 2026, Harrison had five catches for 85 yards and one touchdown. His trade stock was extremely low, too. According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , one unnamed team speculated that Harrison would only garner a high Day 3 selection.

Instead, the Cardinals secured second- and sixth-round picks, which could be extremely valuable as they consider adding a QB of the future in the 2027 draft.

Considering the other weapons that Arizona has, and the current trajectory of Harrison's NFL stock, the deal is a moderate win for the Cardinals.

The Houston Texans picked up their first win of the season on Sunday, a 26-3 victory over the Tennessee Titans. While 1-4 franchises usually aren't buyers at the trade deadline, this deal still makes sense for Houston.

Specifically, it makes a ton of sense for Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud.

Stroud became extension-eligible this offseason, though Houston has had no real reason to give him a second contract early. While Stroud was electric as the 2023 Offensive Rookie of the Year, he largely regressed over the past two seasons. However, he's been impressive again this year, despite Houston's rocky start to the season.

The former Buckeyes quarterback came into Week 5 with 1,141 passing yards, five touchdowns, no interceptions, and a 95.9 quarterback rating. Against Tennessee, he racked up another 261 passing yards and a touchdown to go with a 107.6 rating and a rushing score.

In theory, adding Harrison to the offense will help the Texans build on their first victory of 2026 while helping Stroud continue to develop ahead of a potential offseason contract decision.

Harrison only spent one season as a full-time starter with Stroud at Ohio State, but the two had a fantastic connection that year—Harrison finished 2023 with 1,263 yards and 14 touchdowns. Beyond that, the Texans have long lacked a reliable second target opposite Nico Collins.

Now, betting on Harrison is very much a gamble, considering what he's put on film over the past two years. However, he's still a 24-year-old receiver with elite upside who can be on a rookie deal through 2028—if Houston exercises Harrison's fifth-year option.

Given Harrison's history with Stroud, Houston's need at receiver, and the caliber of pass-catchers likely to be available at this point in the regular season, it's a very smart gamble by the Texans and general manager Nick Caserio.

While this trade could prove to be a smart one for both the Texans and Cardinals, Harrison has to wake up on Monday feeling like he's the biggest winner of the bunch.

The son of Hall of Famer Marvin Harrison Sr. entered the NFL with very lofty expectations, but he also came in with the tools and the intangibles needed to meet them head-on.

"Harrison is a slam-dunk prospect," Derrik Klassen wrote for the Bleacher Report Scouting Department in 2023. "...It's so easy to see how his game translates right away. Harrison would be an instant No. 1 WR for most offenses."

In his two seasons as a go-to target at Ohio State, Harrison certainly looked like a future No. 1 receiver—he topped 1,200 yards with 14 touchdowns in both 2022 and 2023.

While Harrison never developed into a top-tier receiver in Arizona's offense, it's not as if his skill set suddenly disappeared. To get back to being the receiver he was in college, though, he desperately needed a change of scenery .

It's hard to imagine Harrison landing in a much better situation for him. He won't face the pressure of being a top target, and he'll get to play with a quarterback who knows him and what he does well.

"I think he brings a dynamic playmaker, somebody who runs great routes and can catch pretty much any ball. I'm super excited to get to work with him," Stroud said, per Jared Koch of SI.com. "...I'm excited to get him here, get him learning and get him around the other guys. I think it's perfect for him."

Naturally, it'll be up to Harrison himself to mesh with Nick Caley's offense, rekindle his chemistry with Stroud, and finally start playing up to his draft status. However, he should get a fair opportunity to do so in Houston while getting away from the bust label that began to shadow him in Arizona.

articles.title: Commanders coach Dan Quinn and QB Jayden Daniels both accept responsibility for time management gaffe in tie vs. Giants
articles.summary: A Jayden Daniels spike would have set up a 42-yard field goal to win it. The Commanders ran a pass play instead.
articles.body:
The big question from the end of the Washington Commanders' incredible tie on Sunday was, " What were Jayden Daniels and head coach Dan Quinn thinking? " They provided some answers after the game.

A clash with the NFC East rival New York Giants reached the final minute of overtime, when Washington had the ball on second-and-8 in field goal territory with 13 seconds left and no timeouts.

A game-winning field goal would have been roughly 42 yards. Commanders rookie kicker Drew Stevens hasn't missed any of his seven career attempts from inside 50 yards, though he did miss an extra-point attempt earlier in the game.

Calling even a single offensive play in that situation is unimaginably risky, as failing to stop the clock will cost you a chance at that field goal. And yet, the Commanders appeared to call a pass play, then watched in horror as Daniels scrambled, got taken down then couldn't get another play off to spike the ball.

In the well-stocked pantheon of NFL time management gaffes, that is definitely up there. As Quinn's headset can attest.

Quinn immediately took the blame while speaking with reporters after the game, admitting the correct call would have been to simply to stop the clock via a spike or throwaway out of bounds :

"Leaving tonight with a tie feels like a loss. The last sequence — we throw it out of bounds, we clock it, you give yourself a chance to kick it. We pride ourselves on those moments at the end of the game. After the first-down run, still trying to gain more for the kick. Right call is obviously we can go clock it early. Don't put ourselves in that spot, and that's my responsibility, no one else's."

For his part, Daniels didn't offer much clarity when asked what he was trying to do on the fateful play, mostly responding with some form of, "We've just to to be better." He did acknowledge his responsibility, while noting there was some sort of breakdown in communication:

"We've got to stop the clock. We've got to know the situation. We've got to relay that as an offense. It starts with everybody, top down. Ultimately it's on me."

Quinn, however, rejected the idea that Daniels was to blame:

"The sequencing of that does not fall on him. It's an outside throw or a clock. Those are the two, an out-of-bounds throw or a clock. That has to come from me. I don't have to put him into that spot. I can do that earlier. We can finish the kick earlier, we don't need to gain more yards. So that's on me."

Giants head coach John Harbaugh, meanwhile, clearly knew he had gotten away with something .

Ultimately, the play was a failure on both critical fronts, of both concept and execution. Quinn and Daniels both should have understood the resources they were working with and acted accordingly, but the egg is probably going to be more on Quinn's face given that he has the job tasked with making decisions about timeouts and the clock. It's hard to blame Daniels too much for running a play Quinn told him to do, even if the obviously correct course of action was freely available.

It's enough to put Quinn on the hot seat with a 1-3-1 record, if he wasn't there already. And the ending spoiled what could have been a triumphant return for Daniels, who was making his return from a knee injury.

Mike Evans just trolled Trevon Diggs—and then some.

articles.title: Everything Fernando Mendoza Said About Making NFL Debut for Raiders vs. Patriots
articles.summary: Las Vegas Raiders' rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza made his NFL debut in garbage time of Sunday's 45-17 loss against the New England Patriots, finishing 6-of-8 for 48 yards.
articles.body:
Las Vegas Raiders' rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza made his NFL debut in garbage time of Sunday's 45-17 loss against the New England Patriots, finishing 6-of-8 for 48 yards.

After the contest he spoke about taking the field for the first time.

"It wasn't a great experience because of the overall outcome. I wanted to do my part, any way I can help the team. I was called upon and I appreciate all of my teammates, especially some of the starters going out there and having that fighting effort," the top overall pick told reporters . "Entering in what you would call your NFL debut, it's a good experience. Every rookie has it at some point. It was just that time."

"I'm going to keep controlling the controllables, but it is good experience to have some regular-season snaps to go off and evaluate and get better from," Mendoza added.

The Raiders have chosen to roll with Kirk Cousins as the starter thus far in the 2026 season, choosing to bring the 23-year-old Mendoza along slowly. It's felt like a wise approach—despite Sunday's blowout loss the Raiders are 3-2 and Cousins has played well, throwing for 1,269 yards, 12 touchdowns and four interceptions through five games.

It won't be long until Mendoza headlines a burgeoning offense that also includes young stars like Ashton Jeanty and Brock Bowers. But for now, he'll be relegated to getting his reps in practice and in garbage time.

articles.title: 49ers WR Deebo Samuel leaves Seahawks game with hamstring injury in another injury blow to offense
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers are down another key offensive weapon.
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers are down another key offensive weapon.

Wide receiver Deebo Samuel left Sunday's game against the Seattle Seahawks with a hamstring injury in the second half and was quickly ruled out for the rest of the game.

The injury took place in the third quarter as Samuel ran around the edge on a first-down play. As he collapsed, he dropped the ball and fell prone on the field.

It was a frightening moment as Samuel's condition wasn't initially clear. He was able to eventually stand up and limp off the field.

But he clearly wasn't right and clutched his right thigh as he made his way to the sideline. The 49ers announced minutes later that he'd been ruled out of the game with a hamstring injury.

The 49ers also lost wide receiver Jacob Cowing to an ankle injury and listed him as questionable to return.

This is a team that's been beset with injuries at wide receiver since training camp. Starter Ricky Pearsall is out for the season after undergoing preseason surgery to repair a damaged PCL. Standout rookie De'Zhaun Stribling is expected to miss roughly 10 weeks with an ankle injury suffered in San Francisco's Week 1 win over the Los Angeles Rams in Australia .

Demarcus Robinson is on injured reserve with a high-ankle sprain sustained in Week 2's win over the Miami Dolphins . Christian Kirk has been on injured reserve since the preseason with a lingering calf injury.

No. 1 receiver Mike Evans, meanwhile, is playing and thriving through a rib injury he sustained in Week 3 against the Arizona Cardinals.

The 49ers entered Sunday's game at 4-0 despite the injuries and will have to cotinue to play hobbled and shorthanded on offense.

articles.title: It’s Time for NFL Networks to Hire ‘Clock Management’ Specialists
articles.summary: Washington let the clock run out instead of kicking a field goal.
articles.body:
The hiring of Mike Pereira as on-air "rules" analyst by Fox Sports revolutionized sports TV back in 2010. In my book, it's high time for NFL TV partners to add "clock management" analysts to their game telecasts.

Commanders coach Dan Quinn's unforgivable clock management at the end of Sunday's 27–27 tie with the Giants was the biggest clock blunder in years. By inadvertently letting time run out instead of setting up a game-winning field goal, Quinn snatched a tie from the very jaws of victory.

It was so laughable that ProFootballTalk's Mike Florio called it a "firing offense." No wonder, since Washington minority owner Magic Johnson sounded off about the blunder on X/Twitter. "I'm in total disbelief my Commanders had such poor clock management in today's overtime game against the Giants," tweeted Johnson. "All we had to do was kick the field goal and we would have won the game!"

The Magic Man wasn't alone. Fox's play-by-play announcer Chris Myers and color commentator Jonathan Vilma couldn't believe what they were seeing as the Commanders QB Jayden Daniels danced around with no timeouts instead of clocking the ball and attempting a game-winning field goal inside of 40 yards.

"They don't have a timeout. What are they doing?" asked Myers. "They've got to get up and spike this. They're not going to be able to get this done in time! It's gonna run out on them! The clock ran out as Daniels ran the ball!…Unbelievable. A comedy of errors late."

Vilma agreed. "Chris, that's inexcusable!" he said. "It was just supposed to be, you go, you take a knee, set up, clock, and then get out of there."

Across social media, NFL experts registered their shock as the Commanders fell to 1–3–1 and the Giants moved to 3–1–1:

Yahoo's NFL writer Frank Schwab tweeted it wouldn't be a surprise if Quinn–who coughed up a 28–3 lead to Bill Belichick's Patriots in Super Bowl LI–lost his job. "Dan Quinn might not survive this one," he tweeted. "The Commanders had a time management mistake for the ages, costing them a shot at the win."

Ex-Washington quarterback Robert Griffin III was equally aghast. "The Washington Commanders lost because of poor clock management and communication between the coaches and QB Jayden Daniels. IT JUST CAN'T HAPPEN," tweeted RGIII .

Fox's own Tim Brando called it an "inexcusable" miscue, tweeting: "Uhhhh Clock management? @Commanders can we talk? Ouch babe. Great work by my colleague @The_ChrisMyers & @Jonathan_Vilma on what was an inexcusable mistake at the end!

As for hiring "clock management" experts, why not? The NFL's media partners Fox, ESPN, NBC Sports, CBS Sports, and Amazon Prime Video pay anywhere from $1 billion to $2.7 billion a year to show NFL games.

For years, TV viewers have endured example after example of coaches not knowing what to do at crunch time. Hiring a clock management analyst to pop up in the right situation like Pereira would be a logical next step.

Back in 2018, Rams coach Sean McVay hired Jedd Fisch as a clock-management specialist for critical situations. He helped the 15–3 Rams reach Super Bowl LIII. The NFL's media partners should follow McVay's lead.

articles.title: Jahmyr Gibbs Breaks Barry Sanders Touchdown Record
articles.summary: Jahmyr Gibbs broke Barry Sanders' touchdown record before age 25 in the fourth quarter Sunday. #Lions
articles.body:
Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs scored on a 1-yard rushing touchdown in the second quarter to tie Barry Sanders' record for the most touchdowns in the NFL under the age of 25 with 57 (45 rushing and 12 receiving). In the fourth quarter, Gibbs scored on a 3-yard rushing touchdown with 5:03 left in regulation to push Detroit's lead over Arizona to 45-14.

That touchdown broke the record for the most touchdowns in NFL history before age 25. It was No. 58 of Gibbs' career, one clear of Sanders, and Gibbs does not turn 25 until March 20, 2027. Gibbs making history in this game for the Lions is something special.

Gibbs finished the afternoon with 151 rushing yards and two touchdowns on 25 carries, plus five catches for 56 yards, and Detroit won 45-21 to move to 3-2.

Detroit Lions Running Back Jahmyr Gibbs Can Keep Making History This Season

With a bye in Week 6 and 12 games left in the regular season, Gibbs will have the chance to keep adding to his touchdown totals before his 25th birthday. With the way his career is going so far, he has a chance to be one of the all-time Lions greats on the offensive side of the football.

articles.title: Mike Evans’ checked Seahawks defender’s jersey and asked ‘Who Are You?’ in trash talk masterclass
articles.summary: Mike Evans is hilarious.
articles.body:
Mike Evans is new to the rivalry between the San Francisco 49ers and Seattle Seahawks, but he somehow already has one of the best pieces of trash talk in the storied recent history of this matchup. Seattle defensive back Trevon Diggs was talking smack to Evans during the first half of their Week 5 matchup when Evans responded with the nuclear option. As Diggs was chirping away, Evans responded by checking the back of his jersey to send a clear message: I don't even know who you are, and I don't care what you have to say.

Diggs has some name recognition as an eight-year pro who led the NFL in interceptions with the Dallas Cowboys back in 2021, but he's not on Evans' level. This is one of the most disrespectful things I've ever seen on an NFL field. It reminds me of when Aqib Talib snatched Michael Crabtree's chain off his neck . The combination of rudeness and comedic timing here is just perfect. Watch Evans' creative smack talk here:

The fact that Diggs isn't exactly a no-name makes this even funnier. Evans really hit him with the "Who Are You?" before going on with his business.

Evans is having a monster game for the 49ers, which makes this even better. He's over 100 yards and scored the first touchdown of the game. Evans is 33 years old, an age when most receivers have already slowed down, but it feels like he's still as great as ever.

Seahawks-49ers games are always a treat, and trash talk like this makes it even better.

articles.title: “Jason Kelce Talks Nonstop”: Jason Whitlock Posts to Beg Eagles Legend to “Shut Up” During London Game Broadcast
articles.summary: Former ESPN analyst Jason Whitlock seemed unimpressed with Jason Kelce in the broadcast booth for the Jacksonville Jaguars’ 19-17 win over the Philadelphia E...
articles.body:
Former ESPN analyst Jason Whitlock seemed unimpressed with Jason Kelce in the broadcast booth for the Jacksonville Jaguars' 19-17 win over the Philadelphia Eagles in London. The former Eagles center is working as an analyst for NFL Network alongside play-by-play announcer Dave Pasch and Hall of Fame quarterback Kurt Warner. The game is being played at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London.

While the game was going on, Whitlock criticized Kelce for his constant use of "Jesus" while sharing his views on the on-field action.

"What is Jason Kelce doing? Why is he speaking Jesus name in vain during a football broadcast? What was funny? Kurt Warner needs to check him, not laugh it off," Whitlock wrote on X.

A few minutes later, Whitlock called out Kelce for his "non stop" talking.

Finally, when Whitlock got frustrated with Kelce, he wrote:

It's unclear what remarks Kelce made that sparked Whitlock's reactions.

Jason Kelce Covers Eagles For First Time With NFL Network

Jason Kelce has been in the booth for many NFL games, but not the Eagles. Like his brother, Travis Kelce, Jason spent his entire career with only one team. He played 13 seasons for the Eagles from 2011 through 2023. The former sixth-round pick helped the Eagles defeat the New England Patriots 41-33 in Super Bowl LII. His career also included seven Pro Bowl selections.

For the first time since his retirement, Kelce made his first Eagles assignment for NFL Network against the Jaguars on Sunday. He had made his NFL Network debut the previous week , calling the Colts-Commanders game in London on Oct. 4.

During the game, Kelce offered insights. He shed light on Jacksonville's emergency long-snapping situation after Ross Matiscik suffered a shoulder injury. Moreover, when Jaguars defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton stepped in, Kelce explained the challenges of the position from his own experience as a former offensive lineman. A report from OutKick used this as an example to show why the NFL needs more offensive linemen in the booth.

Kelce announced his retirement on March 4, 2024, following the 2023 season.
