articles.title: NFL Week 5 Winners and Losers: Commanders have game-management gaffe for the ages in tie to Giants
articles.summary: The Giants were quite pleased at the end to get the tie.
articles.body:
The worst division in the NFL got a perfectly fitting end to Sunday's game.

The New York Giants celebrated a tie. They should have because the Washington Commanders had a game-management fiasco that will be remembered for a long time.

The Commanders were in field-goal range near the end of an ugly overtime and without any timeouts. Washington took its time to run a final play in the last minute with the clock running. By the time they snapped it and quarterback Jayden Daniels was tackled after running around for a while, there were fewer than 10 seconds left and it wasn't enough time to get lined up and spike the ball (to stop the clock for a game-winning field goal attempt) before the overtime ended.

The Giants and Commanders tied 27-27. It's the kind of mistake that will not get Washington head coach Dan Quinn off the hot seat. It was inexcusable for an NFL team to not get a field-goal attempt off at the end. What happened will be remembered for perhaps the worst clock management error in recent NFL history. The Commanders called a pass play, and Daniels got tackled instead of throwing it away. They needed something that stopped the clock, whether it was a completion near the sideline, a throwaway or any play snapped earlier in which they could have spiked the ball. It was a coaching mistake and Daniels' mistake too.

"Ultimately, you know, it's on me," Daniels told reporters postgame of the mishap.

Quinn said the disaster wasn't on Daniels, admitting that Washington should've spiked the ball instead of run a passing play that had recivers go downfield before time expired.

"Leaving tonight with a tie feels like a loss," Quinn said .

The Dallas Cowboys looked horrendous Thursday night in losing to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and their undrafted rookie quarterback. The Philadelphia Eagles took a brutal walk-off loss in London on Sunday that they might not rebound from, on top of all their injury issues. The Giants are 3-1-1 and they didn't cover themselves in glory on Sunday either.

The unbelievable clock management at the end was the finish of a collapse by the Commanders. The Giants came back after the Commanders took a 27-13 lead in the fourth quarter. New York took the game to overtime on a Malik Nabers touchdown catch with 1:43 left in regulation. New York got the ball first in overtime but Dominic Zvada pushed a field goal wide left. The Commanders punted after their drive stalled and they took a delay of game penalty on fourth-and-5. The Giants drove into field-goal range but Cam Skattebo lost a fumble. It was ugly, even before the final minute.

The Commanders strung together some plays and looked to be in position to kick a field goal but managed to run a play with 55 seconds left, stand around waiting for the next play, snap it again with 12 seconds left and then run out of time before they could spike the ball to get the field-goal team on.

The Giants aren't pretty but everyone else in the NFC East is uglier. New York needed last-second interceptions in or near their own end zone to win home games over the Titans and Cardinals the last two weeks. Sunday's comeback to tie was impressive in some ways but they also fumbled away a shot at the win in overtime, as well as missed a field goal in the extra period. But a half-win seemed like a win, after the Commanders were in position for a field-goal try. But thanks to Quinn, Daniels and a horrible mishap, we'll never find out if that field goal would have been good.

Here are the rest of the winners and losers from Week 5 of the NFL season:

San Francisco 49ers: The NFC West game between two of the best teams in the NFL had plenty of mistakes. There were key penalties and seven turnovers. Neither team played their best.

It was still high drama between the San Francisco 49ers and Seattle Seahawks. And the 49ers left no doubt they are the No. 1 team in football after five weeks with a dramatic 32-29 win.

The 49ers took a 32-29 lead with 1:56 left on a field goal. Jaxon Smith-Njigba immediately got a 35-yard catch to get the Seahawks to midfield. But then, on a third-and-10, Smith-Njigba had a drop. It wasn't an easy catch but it hit his hands, and it's rare to see JSN not make the play. On fourth down Cooper Kupp tried diving for the first down but was marked a yard short as he dove near the sideline. The play was reviewed and the call on the field stood. The 49ers had the win.

The 49ers started 4-0, but hadn't played a true road game and had a couple easy opponents. Sunday was a true test. It wasn't always clean for them. But Mike Evans had a huge day with 113 yards and a touchdown, Brock Purdy made some big plays and the defense forced two turnovers including a massive one by rookie defensive lineman Gracen Halton when he stripped George Holani in the final seconds of the end of the first half and recovered in the end zone.

The 49ers are 5-0 and the top team in football so far. They left no debate about that on Sunday afternoon.

Detroit Lions defense: The Lions came into Sunday's game ranked last in many defensive statistics. They were awful on Sunday night last week against the Carolina Panthers.

The Lions defense had a solid game and the offense played to its usual standard in a blowout 45-21 win over the Arizona Cardinals. The Cardinals have plenty of stars at the skill positions but didn't do much offensively until the outcome of the game was decided. The Lions led 31-7 with five minutes left in the third quarter, when Arizona started to get some meaningless yards and a couple scores.

The Lions got another monster game from Jahmyr Gibbs (207 total yards, two touchdowns) and Jared Goff played well too with 271 yards and three passing touchdown with a rushing touchdown on a quarterback sneak thrown in. That's to be expected. For the Lions to be anything more than a fringe playoff contender it needs the defense to regularly start playing like it did Sunday at Arizona.

Kyler Murray: When the Minnesota Vikings finally got Murray and Justin Jefferson healthy for a full game, their offense didn't look quite as bad.

Minnesota had its best offensive game of the season in a 23-13 win over the New Orleans Saints , which pushes their record to 5-0. Murray was efficient with 229 passing yards and another 51 rushing. Jefferson, coming off an ankle injury, had a great touchdown catch with three defenders around him in the end zone.

Murray was knocked out in the first game of the season due to a concussion. In the first half of his first game back, Jefferson suffered an ankle injury. Sunday was the first time they played a full game together. Minnesota's offense looked much better. Its defense continued its run as perhaps the best in the NFL this season. And the Vikings' lead in the NFC North continues to grow.

Houston Texans' defense: It's not hard to shut down the Tennessee Titans' offense this season. But the Texans still needed a game like Sunday.

The winless Texans, coming off a defensive letdown that led to a Cowboys victory, weren't going to let it be a close game against the Titans. They looked like the defense everyone expected to see before the season started, as they clamped down on the Titans for a 26-3 win . Tennessee finished with 187 yards and scored only a field goal.

The Texans are 1-4, and while that isn't a good place to be my any means, it's better than 0-5. Houston needed a win and the defense showed up for it.

Drake Maye: Maybe all the talk of Maye being a below average quarterback was an overreaction.

Maye was never as bad as he looked in some tough games last postseason and to start this season, and now it looks like he's back. Maye carved up the Las Vegas Raiders and the New England Patriots had an easy 45-17 win . Maye had 374 yards and four touchdowns passing with another 25 yards and a touchdown on the ground. The blowout Sunday was the Patriots' second straight win. Last week the Patriots beat the Buffalo Bills with Maye playing well.

Maye came within one vote of winning NFL MVP last season. Patriots haters were quick to pile on when he started slowly this season. It appears the slump is over.

David Bailey: The New York Jets had a difficult decision with the No. 2 overall pick of the NFL Draft. Many thought they'd take Ohio State linebacker Arvell Reese due to his upside. Instead they took Bailey out of Texas Tech. It's working out pretty well.

Bailey had a massive game as the New York Jets got an ugly 17-12 win over the Cleveland Browns on Sunday . New York won after Cleveland flubbed a punt snap and the Jets recovered in Browns territory, then Braelon Allen scored on a 22-yard touchdown to give the Jets the lead. New York's defense held on after that.

Bailey had three sacks. The Browns were 3-1 coming in but their offense got shut down by the Jets, who were led by their rookie pass rusher.

Bailey was a fantastic pass rusher in college and that has translated to the NFL. He had two sacks in his first four games and then had a breakout in his fifth game. The Jets have a foundational piece for their defense.

Justin Herbert: Herbert has to take the blame for most of the Los Angeles Chargers' struggles this season. He hasn't played well.

But Sunday, there wasn't much he could do. The Chargers lost 23-17 to the Denver Broncos to fall to 0-5 and it was a rough day for Herbert with a skeleton crew around him.

Herbert was playing with a preseason offensive line due to injuries, which included both tackles Joe Alt and Rashawn Slater. He was without receivers Ladd McConkey, who was active but didn't play, and Tre Harris, who suffered a hamstring injury in the first half. Herbert didn't surpass 100 yards passing until the final minute of Sunday's game. He was sacked five times, losing a crucial fumble on one, and threw an interception. He was sacked on the final play of the game when the Chargers had a chance to throw it to the end zone.

It looked like last season when Herbert had to do it all himself due to injuries, only with many more injuries around him and way worse results.

Ben Johnson: Matt LaFleur got a little revenge on Sunday.

The Green Bay Packers head coach has been criticized and Johnson is a big reason for it. Johnson came into the head coaching job of the Chicago Bears with bravado, saying he was going to like beating LaFleur twice a year, then had two massive wins over the Packers last season, including a playoff victory. When Johnson won games with Case Keenum and Tyson Bagent replacing Caleb Williams the past couple weeks, the hype around Johnson got even stronger.

Johnson was humbled a little bit on Sunday. Jordan Love had a huge game with 367 yards and two touchdowns, a Packers defense that hadn't been playing well shut down Bagent and the Bears' offense and Green Bay got its best win of the season as it blew out Chicago 31-7 .

Johnson started Bagent over Keenum, even though Keenum was very good in his one start against the Eagles, and maybe there is some second-guessing that can be done there . Or, the lesson is, it's just hard to win on the road with a backup quarterback in the NFL no matter who it is. But Packers fans will be happy to take a victory lap regardless of the circumstances.

Malik Willis: He has almost nothing to work with on the Miami Dolphins offense, especially since De'Von Achane is done for the season with a torn ACL. But he also hasn't done anything to let the Dolphins know they can bypass a quarterback in the 2027 NFL Draft.

Willis is probably going to be graded by the Dolphins on a curve due to the situation he's in, but he still needs to play better than this. With a minute to go in the first half against the Cincinnati Bengals, Willis was 1-of-7 passing for 22 yards. No matter who you're throwing to, that's not good enough. Willis rallied after that, finishing with 137 passing yards, but he had two interceptions and the Bengals won 31-24 .

Willis signed a three-year, $67.5 million contract in the offseason and it was a fine gamble from a Miami team that had no hope coming into the season. The Dolphins can easily get out of the deal after two years. They took a shot, after Willis played well as the Packers' backup in limited starts, that they could find their franchise quarterback in free agency. It's not working out that way yet.

Colts GM Chris Ballard: The Indianapolis Colts' roster is flawed on both sides of the ball. A quarterback they drafted fourth overall three years ago, Anthony Richardson Sr., looks like a bust as he backs up Daniel Jones. When the Colts signed receiver Alec Pierce to a four-year, $114 million deal it was shocking, and Pierce has 72 yards this season and is on injured reserve.

Colts head coach Shane Steichen gets a lot of attention for his time on the hot seat, but Ballard is there too. The general manager of the Colts has overseen a roster that isn't good enough. The Colts lost 34-22 to the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday to fall to 2-3 . The defense allowed Jaylen Warren to score on an 80-yard touchdown pass and a 50-yard touchdown run. The offense was OK, but Jonathan Taylor and Jones combined for zero touchdowns.

Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon let it be known after last season that everyone was on notice coming into this season. It's not starting well for Steichen or Ballard.

Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni: It'll be tough for the Philadelphia Eagles coach to bounce back from this one.

The Eagles seemingly had a massive 17-16 win against the Jacksonville Jaguars on a Jake Elliott field goal with eight seconds left. But, there were eight seconds left. The Eagles kicked off and allowed Ameer Abdullah to return it 53 yards, giving Cam Little a chance for a 57-yard field goal. It was astounding that the Eagles allowed the Jaguars that chance to return the kick, especially considering they allowed a kickoff return for a touchdown on the opening play, though it was negated due to a penalty . The Jaguars lost their long snapper to an injury early in the game and the snap was high, but Little still hit the game-winning field goal. The Jaguars won 19-17 .

For a moment it looked like a great win for the Eagles, who were heavily shorthanded due to injuries and right tackle Lane Johnson's retirement. Jalen Hurts came through with a drive in the final two minutes without much help around him. Elliott's field goal was clutch. But it ended in a massive disappointment, a long flight home and more questions about Sirianni after Philadelphia's 2-3 start.

articles.title: 49ers Beat Seahawks, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Purdy, Darnold, CMC, JSN, Kupp, Top Players
articles.summary: In a battle of two Super Bowl contenders and division rivals, the San Francisco 49ers downed the defending champion Seattle Seahawks 29-26 on Sunday.
articles.body:
In a battle of two Super Bowl contenders and division rivals, the San Francisco 49ers downed the defending champion Seattle Seahawks 29-26 on Sunday.

A tight battle between the NFC West foes came down to the final moments, and the game was ultimately decided by a field goal from the Niners. San Francisco stayed undefeated with the win, while Seattle dropped to 3-2.

The Niners went three-and-out on their opening drive, but came up with an interception on Seattle's opening drive. San Francisco capitalized when Brock Purdy found Mike Evans in the end zone, but the Seahawks later answered with a short rushing score from Emanuel Wilson.

Seattle took a momentary lead in the second quarter, but Christian McCaffrey scored on the following drive to put the Niners back on top, 14-10.

The Seahawks cut into the lead with another field goal from Jason Myers to make it a 14-13 game halfway through the second quarter and they looked like they were going to go into halftime trailing by just a point.

But San Francisco's defense stepped up in the final seconds of the quarter, forcing a fumble and recovering it in the end zone.

Seattle then had more offensive woes to start the second half when Sam Darnold threw his second interception, but he quickly corrected course and helped get his team back in the game.

Jaxson Smith-Njigba scored a 16-yard touchdown pass from Darnold, and Myers hit a pair of field goals to give Seattle a 26-21 lead heading into the final quarter.

The Niners struck back to start the fourth quarter, scoring on a touchdown pass from Purdy to the newest Niner, Brandin Cooks. The 49ers converted the two-point conversion to go up by three.

The Seahawks once again tied things up with a field goal, but San Francisco regained the lead with a field goal of its own on the following drive, leaving Seattle with just under two minutes to answer.

The field goal proved to be the decider.

Seattle had the chance for a big play, but a rare drop from Smith-Njigba brought up fourth down. Cooper Kupp nearly converted on fourth down, but was just short.

The first meeting between the 49ers and Seahawks this year delivered, and it won't be surprising to see another exciting battle in November.

articles.title: Updated 2027 NFL Draft Order After Week 5 Results, Who Could Titans & Chargers Take?
articles.summary: The three remaining winless teams in the NFL are the favorites to land the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL draft after Week 5.
articles.body:
The three remaining winless teams in the NFL are the favorites to land the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL draft after Week 5.

The Tennessee Titans, Los Angeles Chargers and Miami Dolphins occupy the first three spots in the projected draft order.

There doesn't seem to be much hope in sight for any of those three teams, so they may all be at the forefront of the No. 1 pick battle for the foreseeable future.

Five teams left Week 5 with just one victory. They are still very much in the running for the top pick as well, but at least right now, there's a clear hierarchy in the race to be the league's worst team.

11. New York Jets (via Indianapolis - 2-3)

C.J. Carr played his way into the conversation of top quarterbacks to be drafted in April.

The Notre Dame signal-caller has 16 touchdown passes and a single interception through six games.

Carr threw for at least 230 yards in five of his six games and owns a 70.8 completion percentage.

The Titans are still committed to Cam Ward, but if things continue to not go well, they at least have to explore the deep quarterback draft pool.

Carr is one of many potential options, along with Arch Manning, Dante Moore and Darian Mensah among others that should be first-round picks in April.

The Chargers will probably try to add help around Justin Herbert, but the Dolphins could be in the quarterback market to take the next step in their rebuild.

It may be hard for anyone to match Colin Simmons as the top defensive prospect in the 2027 draft class.

Simmons had two more sacks on Saturday in the Texas Longhorns' loss to the Oklahoma Sooners.

Simmons is up to 9.5 sacks and 12 solo tackles through six games for the previous No. 1-ranked team in the country.

If the Titans, Chargers or Dolphins don't go the quarterback route, Simmons should be at, or near, the top of their draft boards.

An argument can be made that Simmons could make the biggest impact on a team out of the 2027 draft class. Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith is also in that discussion.

Regardless, Simmons should be in the top five or top 10 conversation because of how impactful he can be on defense.

articles.body:
On Sunday, a report emerged that the Arizona Cardinals refused to provide wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. with a Seeker machine, which is essentially a robotic quarterback.

And former NFL head coach Marvin Lewis said on social media that Harrison ultimately bought his own Jugs machine, since the Cardinals didn't have one:

Harrison, 54, has long had a rigorous training routine that includes a heavy Jugs workout. As ESPN reported back in 2024, "Harrison catches about 200 balls before practice Monday, Tuesday and Saturday and after practice on Wednesdays, Thursdays and Fridays" which is "in addition to the hours of work he puts in on his body—recovering, lifting and getting treatment—the playbook and his craft."

The Cardinals failing to provide a Seeker machine perhaps contributed to the disconnect that ultimately resulted in the team trading him to the Houston Texans on Sunday, just two years after making him the No. 4 overall pick in the NFL draft.

Hopefully the Texans are willing to invest in a Seeker machine.

articles.title: Week 6 Waiver Wire Breakout Fantasy Football Pickups from Sunday's Box Scores
articles.summary: Unfortunately, the trend in waiver-wire pickup advice so far this season has been targeting whichever backup running back is moving into the main role following an injury to the starter (see: Ollie Gordon, Miami Dolphins; Tank Bigsby and then Will Shipley, Philadelphia Eagles; Braelon Allen, New York Jets).
articles.body:
Unfortunately, the trend in waiver-wire pickup advice so far this season has been targeting whichever backup running back is moving into the main role following an injury to the starter (see: Ollie Gordon , Miami Dolphins; Tank Bigsby and then Will Shipley, Philadelphia Eagles; Braelon Allen, New York Jets).

While these are savvy moves for fantasy managers to make, it's much more fun to witness a player have a breakout game or string together big performances and submit a claim hoping not to plug a temporary hole but deepen a bench or flex slot for the rest of the season.

The three players we're looking at today have all finally capitalized on the opportunities they've been given (and, in some cases, their teams have finally given them the opportunities they deserve).

Points use PPR scoring. Scoring and rostered data via FantasyPros .

Week 5 stats: 10 att, 31 rush yd, 2 rush TD, 1 rec, 6 rec yds, 16.2 pts

Savvy fantasy managers picked up MarShawn Lloyd on waivers after Josh Jacobs landed on the Commissioner's Exempt List. However, many of them have since dropped him; not surprising given that he has failed to reach the 10-point in any game this season.

That all changed in Sunday's statement win over the archrival Chicago Bears. The Packers never trailed at any point, which allowed head coach Matt LaFleur to successfully run his play-action heavy offense. It also meant Green Bay wasn't forced into a pass-heavy game to make up a large deficit.

These conditions made for a fantastic day for Lloyd. Yes, his 16.2 points were padded by two rushing touchdowns, but LaFleur got Lloyd in the run and passing games and considered him a go-to red-zone option.

Week 7 is the first that Jacobs could possibly return, so this is the time to submit a claim for Lloyd in what may be his biggest game of the season in Week 6.

Week 5 stats: 5 rec, 44 yds, 2 rec TD, 19.0 pts

Pat Freiermuth has always been a touchdown-dependent fantasy tight end, and that hasn't necessarily changed. The 19 points he scored in Sunday's win over the Indianapolis Colts was bolstered by two trips to the end zone.

However, Freiermuth had a sizable contribution in the passing game as well, totaling 44 yards on five receptions. He was targeted seven times, the most all season.

Freiermuth is still part of an offense where he splits snaps with tight end Darnell Washington. But having scored four touchdowns across five games so far this season, if you have an underperforming tight end on your roster, Freiermuth is looking more and more like a starting-caliber option in deep leagues.

Week 5 stats: 5 rec, 41 yds, 1 rec TD, 12.7 pts

Houston Texans young wideout Jaylin Noel may still be considered a deep-league flex option heading into Week 6, but with two big games in a row, this could be the week your opponents are looking to submit a waiver-wire claim for him.

Noel followed up his 11.9-point outing in Week 4 with another double-digit points day. He brought in all five of his targets against the Tennessee Titans on Sunday, the most he's seen this season. Sunday also marked the third consecutive game that Noel had above a 55% route share.

Noel appears to be limited only by how much offensive coordinator Nick Caley and head coach DeMeco Ryans want to get him involved in the offense. The Texans don't have many weapons to speak of behind Nico Collins, and Noel has made the most of the opportunities he's gotten this season. If Week 6 sees him continue to progress, you'll want him on your roster, not your opponent's.

articles.title: Jahmyr Gibbs Breaks Barry Sanders' NFL Record with 2-TD Game vs. Cardinals
articles.summary: Jahmyr Gibbs is very quickly becoming a Detroit legend.
articles.body:
Jahmyr Gibbs is very quickly becoming a Detroit legend.

The Lions' superstar running back broke another Detroit legend's record on Sunday after scoring his 58th touchdown before turning 25 years old, the most in NFL history:

Gibbs still has a long way to go before he can match Sanders' 15,269 rushing yards (fourth in NFL history) or 99 touchdowns on the ground (11th all time).

But he's already the most dynamic running back the team has had since Sanders. It takes a special talent to evoke the name of Sanders in Detroit, but Gibbs is already doing so.

articles.title: C.J. Stroud Hypes Marvin Harrison Jr. After Texans-Cardinals Trade Reunites Former OSU Teammates
articles.summary: Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud is very familiar with his newest wide receiver.
articles.body:
Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud is very familiar with his newest wide receiver.

Marvin Harrison Jr., whom the Texans acquired from the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday, played alongside Stroud at Ohio State. Stroud hyped his new target following the trade.

"I think he brings a dynamic playmaker. Somebody who runs great routes, can catch really any ball. I loved him in college," Stroud told reporters. "Probably the hardest worker I've ever been around in my life. And who he is off the field, he's a great dude, quiet guy but defintley you feel his presence. I'm excited to get him in here and get him learning & get him around the other guys. It's perfect for him, I think fresh starts are good. I'm excited to get him with us."

Texans' Fantasy Outlook With MHJ, Stroud

The Cardinals traded Harrison and a seventh-round pick to the Texans in return for a 2027 second-round pick and a sixth-round pick. The move came just over two years after Arizona drafted Harrison fourth overall after his tremendous college career.

Harrison hasn't had the start to his career that he hoped for, and he's played a small role for the Cardinals to start the year. In four games, he had just five receptions for 85 yards and a touchdown.

But joining a new team could help Harrison kickstart his career after the slow start, and being alongside his former quarterback could be the perfect situation for him.

Stroud and Harrison were dominant during the 2022 season in Columbus. That year, Harrison had 1,263 yards and 14 touchdowns, and Stroud threw for 3,688 yards, 41 touchdowns and six interceptions.

In their final game together, Harrison had 106 yards and two touchdowns in the College Football Playoff semifinal against George before suffering a concussion on a hit to the end in the end zone.

Ohio State led 35-24 late in the third quarter when Harrison was injured. The Buckeyes were outscored 18-3 after that and ultimately fell after missing a last-second field. After Ohio State lost that game, Stroud and Harrison have now unfinished business to attend to.

The Texans started the season 0-4 before finally getting their first win of the year against the Tennessee Titans on Sunday.

Houston has its work cut out for it trying to get back into the playoff race, but perhaps the duo of Stroud and Harrison can right the ship.

articles.title: Jim Harbaugh Takes Blame for Broncos Loss as Chargers Drop to 0-5, Talks Justin Herbert's Struggles
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Chargers are off to their worst start in decades after a loss to the Denver Broncos on Sunday.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Chargers are off to their worst start in decades after a loss to the Denver Broncos on Sunday.

Amid the 0-5 start, Jim Harbaugh is taking the blame. The head coach took ownership of several late miscues, as well as quarterback Justin Herbert's struggles.

There's plenty wrong with the Chargers amid the 0-5 start, but their offense has been by far the weakest link. Sunday marked Herbert's worst game of the season as he threw for just 121 yards, a touchdown and an interception.

Despite the lackluster game from Herbert, the Chargers were on the brink of a big win over a divisional foe. They trailed by just three points late in the fourth quarter and had the chance to tie or take the lead, but their drive quickly ended. Herbert threw an interception and gave the ball back to Denver near the red zone.

While Los Angeles' defense prevented a touchdown, the Broncos went up by six points on a field goal.

Herbert had one last chance to lead a game-winning drive and got the Chargers into Denver territory, but he took a sack and time expired.

"We gotta do whatever we can to win football games and make plays and do what we can to score points, and we haven't been doing that," Herbert told reporters . "We gotta do that better."

The Chargers appeared to be a team on the rise with Harbaugh at the helm and Herbert under center, reaching the playoffs in back-to-back seasons. They came into this year as a potential Super Bowl contender.

Now, Los Angeles would be lucky to even make the playoffs, and it could lead to drastic changes at the end of the season.

articles.title: Sauce Gardner Responds to DK Metcalf's Viral Comments on Video After Colts' Loss to Steelers
articles.summary: Pittsburgh Steelers' wideout DK Metcalf made some headlines before Sunday's win over the Indianapolis Colts, pretending like he wasn't familiar with star cornerback Sauce Gardener and saying he doesn't "worry about what a DB does well—they've got to guard me."
articles.body:
Pittsburgh Steelers' wideout DK Metcalf made some headlines before Sunday's win over the Indianapolis Colts, pretending like he wasn't familiar with star cornerback Sauce Gardener and saying he doesn't "worry about what a DB does well—they've got to guard me."

Gardner had his own thoughts on the pregame shade following the loss.

"I [saw the comments]. Quite a few people from Detroit sent me that," he told reporters. "They got the win today. They're a pretty good team. We've just gotta be better. Hats off to them for getting the win, but we gotta be better. ... I play corner, so you know how that goes. I don't want to feed too much into it. I don't want it to be bigger than what it's supposed to be. Yeah, it is what it is."

While Pittsburgh indeed won the matchup, 34-22, Metcalf was held to just three receptions for 12 yards and one run for 11 yards. It was a "lost the battle, won the war" type of day for the wideout.

articles.title: The 49ers look like the NFL’s best team after surviving a heavyweight fight
articles.summary: Behind quarterback Brock Purdy, the San Francisco 49ers beat the Seattle Seahawks on the road — and appear to be the NFL’s best team through five weeks.
articles.body: The last time San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy played in Seattle, he could lead an injury-laden 49ers team to only two field goals in a 35-point playoff loss to the Super Bowl-bound Seahawks. On Sunday, Purdy led San Francisco to a game-winning drive in the fourth quarter of a 32-29 win, handing Seattle its first home loss in 371 days. Is San Francisco headed to the Super Bowl next? There’s a long way to go, but the 49ers are 5-0 for the third time under coach Kyle Shanahan — and the last two times they were still playing in February. Sunday’s game was an instant classic, a matchup filled with wild moments and playoff intensity. The teams combined for a whopping seven turnovers and multiple personal fouls, and one player — San Francisco linebacker Dre Greenlaw — was even ejected. The defenses largely dominated until the fourth quarter. That was when Purdy, perhaps the MVP favorite through the first four weeks and change of the NFL season, stepped up. Trailing 26-21, Purdy led the 49ers on a 12-play, 74-yard touchdown drive that culminated in a 7-yard touchdown pass to Mike Evans. Purdy then threw to Evans again to convert a 2-point attempt to put San Francisco ahead 29-26. After a Seattle field goal, the 49ers traveled 43 yards in eight plays for a 44-yard field goal that proved to be the game winner. “I thought Brock did an unbelievable job finding a way there to win at the end,” Shanahan said. “There were some ups and downs. By no means was everything perfect. He was really good in the fourth quarter.” On the Seahawks’ final possession, the offense couldn’t convert a fourth-and-10 — though whether receiver Cooper Kupp was able to stretch the ball for a first down on the play seemed up for debate. While neither quarterback was great Sunday, Purdy had some impressive moments considering the circumstances. Facing the NFL’s second-best defense in expected points added per play, Purdy capitalized on early turnovers before he managed the two scoring drives in the fourth. And he did so with a depleted receiving corps. The 49ers entered Sunday with four receivers on injured reserve. Then Deebo Samuel and Jacob Cowing were injured during the game. “We got a bunch of warriors,” Shanahan said of the backups who stepped up. “Everyone knows the talent and the stars of some of the guys on our team. What makes our guys special is how much they love football, how much they give it up every week.” Among those who played key roles Sunday was Evans, who caught a season-high seven passes for 113 yards and a score, plus the 2-pointer for good measure. “He’s a game-changer,” Purdy said. “As a quarterback, any time I have to go to him it always feels good.” Evans told Fox after the game: “We knew it was going to be a dogfight. They’re a great team, and we came out here and showed we’re a great team, as well.” Purdy finished with a so-so stat line by his standards: 19 of 29 passing for 189 yards, two touchdowns and one interception. More important, though, he outplayed his counterpart, Sam Darnold, and found a way to shepherd two go-ahead drives in the game’s biggest moments. The 49ers now have the league’s most impressive résumé through five weeks. San Francisco has the best point differential in the NFL, and three of its five wins have come against teams with winning records. And two of those wins came against teams that are both legitimate championship contenders and divisional rivals: Seattle and the Los Angeles Rams. Purdy has been spectacular this season. After the Week 5 win, he has now thrown for 13 touchdowns and only two interceptions. Sunday’s game was the only one this season in which he has posted a passer rating under 100, and he still posted a mark of 92.5. The 49ers have done all of that despite being beset with injuries. While the Seahawks were down some of their own key players Sunday, San Francisco ultimately pulled out an ugly win on the road against a team that hadn’t lost at home in over a year — a sign of how much stronger the 49ers look compared with a season ago.

articles.title: Marvin Harrison Jr. Trade to Texans Explained by Cardinals HC, NFL Rumors Weren't 'Distraction'
articles.summary: The Arizona Cardinals drafted Marvin Harrison Jr. fourth overall in 2024, hoping the receiver could be the team's offensive weapon as they continued their rebuild.
articles.body:
The Arizona Cardinals drafted Marvin Harrison Jr. fourth overall in 2024, hoping the receiver could be the team's offensive weapon as they continued their rebuild.

On Sunday, they traded him to the Houston Texans.

Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur discussed the trade after Sunday's loss to the Detroit Lions, saying it was "in the best interest of the club." He added that the timing of the trade wasn't a factor in the loss to the Lions.

"I don't think it was a distraction at all," he told reporters . "It's not why we didn't play well today."

Harrison had a promising rookie year with the Cardinals, recording 885 yards and eight touchdowns, but he didn't show much improvement in Year 2, recording 608 yards and four touchdowns in 12 games.

Through the first four games this year, Harrison was barely a part of the offense. He had just five receptions for 85 yards and a touchdown.

Given his small role on offense, it's fair to wonder whether Harrison was hoping to be traded.

"I'm not gonna answer for Marv," LaFleur said.

LaFleur, the former offensive coordinator of the Los Angeles Rams, said before the season that he envisioned Harrison in a Davante Adams-like role in Arizona. On Sunday, he didn't offer an explanation as to why Harrison didn't plan out with the Cardinals.

"I'm not gonna totally get into that right now. I really like Marvin Harrison. He's a good person. I wish him well," LaFleur said. "We did what we thought was in the best interest of the Cardinals. Any guy that does not play to the level that I feel like they're capable of, I'm always gonna put that on me and coaching in general."

Changing teams might be exactly what Harrison needs to turn into the receiver the Cardinals thought he could be when they drafted him. He should play a big role in Houston and will get to team up with his former college quarterback, C.J. Stroud.

For Arizona, it's clear there are a few years of rebuilding ahead, and getting some picks in return for Harrison will help speed up the process.

articles.title: Justin Herbert’s nightmare continues as Chargers lose again, but benching their $52.5 million QB isn’t the answer
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-5 for the first time since 2003, and Sunday hurt more than most losses.
articles.body: The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-5 for the first time since 2003, and Sunday hurt more than most losses. They led the Denver Broncos by seven in the fourth quarter at SoFi Stadium, then gave up the final 13 points in a 23-17 defeat. Jim Harbaugh pointed the finger at himself afterward. Justin Herbert, the $52.5 million quarterback, is still absorbing most of the outside criticism, and calls to bench him are getting louder. The game, and the four before it, show why sitting him would be the wrong move.Should the Chargers bench Justin Herbert after the 0-5 start?Benching a franchise quarterback shapes the next five years, not the next five Sundays. Justin Herbert has not been sharp. Through four games he had completed 71 of 119 passes for 816 yards, with four touchdowns and six interceptions. NFL.com noted he was the first Chargers quarterback since Ryan Leaf in 2000 to reach six picks and 10 sacks that quickly. Those numbers are ugly. They also describe a passer who spends most snaps running for his life. Harbaugh has backed him all season, saying he respects no player he has coached more than Herbert.Sunday offered a fairer read.On third-and-seven at the Denver 30, Herbert slipped out of a muddy pocket, shook one defender, stiff-armed another and gained 23 yards. Two plays later he hit Hayden Rucci in the back of the end zone for the first Chargers touchdown. Los Angeles led 17-10. Then the game flipped. A fourth-down stuff, a lost fumble and an interception, all inside the Chargers' own 40, handed Denver three short fields and 13 points, the last a 19-yard Wil Lutz field goal with 5:07 left.Harbaugh owned it. He said he saw the Broncos tighten up before the fourth-down snap and wished he had called timeout and punted. "It was the wrong decision," he said.Why won't benching Herbert fix the Chargers offense?The bigger problem sits in front of him.Rashawn Slater and Joe Alt, the starting tackles, both went down against Seattle last week. Slater is expected to land on injured reserve with a high ankle sprain, and four rookies played on the line that day. Herbert was also the second-most sacked quarterback in the league last season. Denver got to him five times Sunday. A backup would face the same rush behind the same blockers.Seattle showed the pattern. The Chargers outgained the Seahawks 301 yards to 286 and still lost 30-23 after four turnovers and 16 penalties. Sunday brought a 237-224 yardage edge and another loss. That looks like a team beating itself.None of this lets Herbert off the hook. He has to protect the ball better, even when the pocket collapses. His opening-play interception against Seattle was the kind of gift opponents do not need. articles.title: Aaron Rodgers Passes Peyton Manning on TD List, QB Reacts to Historic Feat After Steelers Beat Colts
articles.summary: Returning for another season at 42 years old means Aaron Rodgers has the chance to bolster his historic resume even further, and he did just that on Sunday.
articles.body:
Returning for another season at 42 years old means Aaron Rodgers has the chance to bolster his historic resume even further, and he did just that on Sunday.

The Pittsburgh Steelers collected his 580th career touchdown pass, breaking a tie with Peyton Manning on the NFL's all-time passing touchdowns list (including playoffs). Rodgers now holds sole possession of third place on the list, just behind Tom Brady and Drew Brees.

"Anytime you're in the same sentence as Peyton, that definitely does mean a lot to me," Rodgers said.

Rodgers' 580th touchdown fittingly came against the Indianapolis Colts, where Manning spent the bulk of his Hall of Fame career. He connected with running back Jaylen Warren for an explosive 80-yard touchdown, getting the pass off while taking a big hit.

"I think I earned that one because I took a shot from Grover (Stewart) on the play," Rodgers said.

The touchdown was the first of three for Rodgers, who had 235 yards in a 34-22 win over the Colts.

The Steelers moved to 3-2 with the win as Rodgers looks to finish off his legendary career with a big season.

Rodgers likely won't catch up to Brees for second place, barring an outstanding finish to the year, but moving into third place on the list is just another testament to how much of an impact Rodgers has had throughout his career.

articles.title: Without Lamar Jackson, Ravens get a huge comeback win over Falcons behind Tyler Huntley
articles.summary: The Ravens were without their star quarterback, Lamar Jackson, on Sunday night.
articles.body: The Baltimore Ravens didn't have Lamar Jackson on Sunday night. That might ultimately be a great thing for their season. The Ravens got a confidence-building win with Tyler Huntley at quarterback. They were without Jackson, who was inactive due to an ankle injury. They trailed the Atlanta Falcons, the hottest team in the NFL over the previous two weeks, by eight points with less than three minutes to go. And they found a way to get a win that can boost a team for a long time. The Ravens tied the game with a touchdown and 2-point conversion with 40 seconds, then went on a long drive to start overtime. Huntley scored on a QB sneak and only 2:57 remained in the extra period. Huntley is IN! The @Ravens complete a 7+ minute drive to start OT 🔥@BALvsATL on NBC/PeacockStream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/f2yhsa2Gi6— NFL (@NFL) October 12, 2026 When the Falcons got their first drive in overtime, Tua Tagovailoa was in at quarterback. Michael Penix Jr. suffered a rib injury on the Falcons' final drive of regulation and was held out for overtime. After one completion, Tagovailoa threw an interception to Kyle Hamilton and the game was over. The Ravens held on for a huge 30-23 win and they're 4-1 to start the season. "Really proud of our team," Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said afterward. "Digging deep, doing whatever it takes to win the game, kind of picking each other up."The Ravens will welcome Jackson back, and they hope it's soon. But Baltimore now knows it's good enough to get a tough road win without its superstar quarterback. Falcons strike firstThe Ravens made a big mistake early and it wasn't because of Huntley. Andrews caught a pass over the middle, had the ball punched out by Falcons safety Sydney Brown and Jessie Bates III scooped it and returned it 36 yards for a touchdown. That came one drive after Andrews dropped what would have been a touchdown pass and the Ravens settled for a field goal. With Jackson out, the other Ravens needed to play well around Huntley, and Andrews wasn't helping. Andrews later had a 2-point conversion punched out of his hands before he secured the catch.The Ravens' defense, however, was locked in early on. Baltimore was the team with the backup quarterback but Penix didn't have a completion until about midway through the second quarter. Even with zero passing yards for a quarter and a half, the Falcons led because of the defensive touchdown. Penix and the Falcons' offense finally got going. Penix hit Drake London for 25 yards, Jahan Dotson for 36 and then he found Kyle Pitts Sr. for a 5-yard touchdown. Despite being very good on defense for most of the first half, the Ravens still trailed 14-9 at halftime. But they stayed in the game, even without Jackson at quarterback. Ravens force overtimeAtlanta tried to get tricky in the third quarter and it cost them. The Falcons had offensive tackle Jake Matthews report as eligible, and snuck him out on a pass route to the end zone. But Matthews couldn't bring in the pass, and the Falcons ended up settling for a field goal. After that Derrick Henry caught an 18-yard touchdown pass out of the backfield. The 2-point conversion failed but the Ravens were back within 17-15. The Falcons added on a couple of field goals in the fourth quarter to take a 23-15 lead with 2:31 to go. The Ravens needed a touchdown and 2-point conversion, and Huntley came through. Huntley quickly got the Ravens into Falcons territory. The drive kept marching on and Huntley hit Devontez Walker for a touchdown with 40 seconds left. Henry took a direct snap into the end zone for the 2-point conversion to tie the game. The Falcons couldn't get in field-goal range — Penix took a big hit on that drive that would knock him out for overtime — and the game went to overtime. Huntley hit a couple of big third-down passes to start overtime. Henry pushed the pile for another first down. Huntley hit Andrews for another first down inside the 10-yard line. The Falcons had to start calling timeouts because Baltimore's drive was taking so much time off the clock. Atlanta's defense couldn't get off the field. Huntley pushed forward for the go-ahead touchdown with 2:57 left in overtime. That was the Ravens' first lead since it was 3-0. Hamilton sealed the win with an interception. The Ravens could look back on Sunday night's win as a big turning point for their season.

articles.title: Ravens Beat Falcons in OT, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Bijan, Henry, Tua, More Amid Penix Injury
articles.summary: Nothing beats Sunday night football going into overtime.
articles.body:
Nothing beats Sunday night football going into overtime.

Tyler Huntley led the Baltimore Ravens to a 30-23 overtime comeback win over the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday night, with Michael Penix Jr. exiting before overtime.

The Falcons entered as 3.5-point home favorites, per FanDuel Sportsbook , and left with a loss at home after giving up 15 points in the fourth and overtime.

The Ravens remained without franchise quarterback Jackson, who suffered an ankle injury in the second quarter of Baltimore's Week 4 win over the Tennessee Titans. Huntley started in his place Sunday.

Baltimore controlled the clock in overtime, taking more than seven minutes on its way to the end zone.

The biggest play of the first quarter came at the 8:03 mark, when Ravens tight end Mark Andrews fumbled at Baltimore's 36-yard line. Falcons safety Jessie Bates III recovered the ball and returned it for a touchdown, giving Atlanta a 7-3 lead after one quarter.

Baltimore added two field goals from 51 yards in the second quarter, but Atlanta halted the momentum with a five-yard touchdown pass from Penix to Kyle Pitts Sr. to take a 14-9 lead into halftime.

Atlanta added a field goal after halftime before Baltimore responded with an 18-yard touchdown pass from Huntley to Derrick Henry. The Ravens cut the deficit to 17-15 after a failed two-point conversion, then forced Atlanta to turn the ball over on downs on its next possession.

Atlanta added two field goals in the fourth quarter to take charge with a 23-15 lead, but Baltimore had their eyes on an exciting finish with 2:31 remaining.

Huntley charged down the field, connecting with Devontez Walker for a touchdown before converting the two-point attempt to tie things up at 23 a piece with 40 seconds left.

It was Atlanta's turn to respond, starting with a big kickoff return and an 18-yard gain on first down. The drive nearly collapsed when the Falcons fumbled, allowing but recovered its blunder. Penix briefly exited with an injury and was replaced by Tua Tagovailoa for one play before returning to lead Atlanta into overtime.

Baltimore opened overtime with a lengthy possession, capped by a Huntley goal-line touchdown to give the Ravens their first lead since the opening drive.

Penix did not return for overtime, with Tagovailoa stepping in at quarterback. He completed a 20-yard pass before Ravens safety Kyle Hamilton intercepted him to seal Baltimore's comeback win.

Atlanta will host the Chicago Bears next Sunday, with Caleb Williams potentially returning from a hamstring injury he suffered in Week 2, per ESPN's Ian Rapoport.

The Ravens will travel to face the Cleveland Browns, with both games scheduled for a 1 p.m. ET kickoff.

articles.title: Michael Penix Jr. Injury, Falcons QB Updates Status and Return Timeline After Tua's Game-Ending INT
articles.summary: Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. suffered a rib injury during the fourth quarter of Sunday's 30-23 overtime loss against the Baltimore Ravens after taking a big hit in the pocket.
articles.body:
Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. suffered a rib injury during the fourth quarter of Sunday's 30-23 overtime loss against the Baltimore Ravens after taking a big hit in the pocket.

Penix—who missed the Falcons' drive in overtime—told reporters after the game, via ESPN's Marc Raimondi , that he doesn't believe it will be a long-term injury.

Henry, Huntley Win the Game for Ravens 🐦‍⬛

Head coach Kevin Stefanski had previously provided more information on the injured quarterback after the contest.

Penix, 26, had a solid game, throwing for 240 yards and a touchdown. But on the final drive in regulation he took a big hit from Tavius Robinson and fumbled, though Atlanta managed to recover the loose ball.

The game then went into overtime and the Ravens scored a touchdown on their first possession. Penix remained on the bench and was replaced by Tua Tagovailoa, who threw a pick on the second play of the drive.

Injuries have been a massive story in Penix's career. The young quarterback only appeared in nine games last season after suffering a left ACL injury that required season-ending surgery. He missed the first two games of the NFL season but provided a spark upon his return, as Atlanta had won two games in a row heading into Sunday night.

Penix also tore his ACL twice in college, and shoulder injuries also cost him significant time at the college level. It's been a bumpy road from a health perspective.

Depending on the severity of this latest injury, Tagovailoa could be called back into action. He was released by the Miami Dolphins ahead of the 2026 campaign after a string of disappointing seasons, though he brings plenty of experience (76 career starts) to the position.

articles.title: Michael Penix Jr. injured late vs. Ravens after big hit; Tua Tagovailoa throws OT interception his place to seal Baltimore's comeback win over Falcons
articles.summary: Michael Penix Jr. took a big hit toward the end of regulation and wasn't able to play in overtime of Sunday's loss to the Baltimore Ravens.
articles.body:
Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. took a big hit toward the end of regulation and wasn't able to play in overtime of Sunday's loss to the Baltimore Ravens due to a rib injury.

He was replaced by backup Tua Tagovailoa, whose second pass as an Atlanta Falcon sealed Baltimore's 30-23 win in overtime . Tagovailoa targeted Drake London on a downfield pass, but found Ravens safety Kyle Hamilton to end the game.

Penix's injury forces Falcons to go to Tua for OT

Penix took the hit in the final seconds of regulation. He immediately clutched his torso as he laid on his back following the hit.

Penix started to get up from the hit that forced a fumble, but couldn't get to his feet. He laid back down on the field before ultimately leaving for the sideline following attention from athletic trainers.

Atlanta recovered the fumble, and Tagovailoa took Penix's place for one play. Penix returned to throw a pass on Atlanta's final offensive play of regulation before a punt ran out the clock and sent the game to overtime tied at 23. It initially appeared as if Penix would be ready to play in overtime.

But as Baltimore milked clock on the first possession of regulation, medical staff continued to speak to Penix on the sideline.

And when the Falcons got the ball with with 2:57 left in overtime following a Ravens touchdown on a Tyler Huntley sneak, Tagovailoa took over at quarterback on the ensuing Atlanta possession. Penix was officially diagnosed with a rib injury.

Tagovailoa's stint lasted exactly two snaps as he threw the interception on Atlanta's second overtime play from scrimmage, and what started as a good night for the Falcons ended in disappointing fashion on two fronts:

The Falcons lost a game they'd led since a first-quarter touchdown until the Ravens' late score to tie it in the final minute of the fourth quarter. And the status of Penix moving forward was unclear.

Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski told reporters postgame that Penix would undergo imaging to determine the severity of the injury.

Per Falcons team reporter Tori McElhaney, Penix said after the game that he initially thought he'd be able to take the field in overtime if the Falcons had the ball first, but that pain set in the longer he sat.

"I hated it," Penix said . "I hated that I couldn't get back in that game."

Penix, whose career has been repeatedly derailed by multiple ACL tears, was playing in his third game this season after missing Atlanta's first two while recovering from his latest ACL injury sustained last season.

Penix helped spark a dormant Falcons offense and led Atlanta to wins over Green Bay and New Orleans in Weeks 3 and 4. Before leaving Sunday's game, Penix had completed 19 of 32 passes for 240 yards with 1 touchdown and no turnovers.

The Falcons are certainly hoping he can return soon with upcoming games against the Bears, 49ers, Buccaneers, Bengals and Chiefs before a Week 11 bye.

articles.title: What do 49ers, Seahawks' first 5 weeks say about their season goals? Why San Francisco sees a risk in 5-0
articles.summary: Niners-Seahawks may not be the loudest the NFC West gets this season even after the game's bevy of takeaways and touchdowns delivered consistent entertainmen...
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers were fresh off their fifth straight win, one of two teams in the NFL to reach that mark on Sunday.

They'd proven not only that they front a diversity of offensive playmakers (hello, 33-year-old Mike Evans) but also that their defense can force the reigning Super Bowl champion into four turnovers — which the Niners promptly converted into 21 points.

So after a 32-29 road win against the division foe that knocked them out of last season's playoffs, why wasn't Christian McCaffrey wary of celebrating?

This wasn't only about the road that still lies ahead.

"Division wins are big," McCaffrey said after contributing 83 yards and a touchdown from scrimmage. "I love our team's mindset: We've been here before, we've been 5-0 and went into the bye 5-3.

"So we're more worried about just continuing to get better."

Cycle back three years, and indeed Kyle Shanahan's squad opened the season 5-0. Quarterback Brock Purdy had thrown nine touchdowns to no interceptions in the opening five-game stretch. The 49ers had trounced the Dallas Cowboys, 42-10, on "Sunday Night Football."

Then losses against the Cleveland Browns, Minnesota Vikings and Cincinnati Bengals followed. The 49ers would make it to 12-5 and a playoff berth, but only after that three-game skid. McCaffrey remembers that as a word of caution to keep heads down. He didn't mention that after that 5-0 became 5-3, the 49ers also would win a divisional-round game and the NFC championship.

Could 5-0 again precede a Super Bowl berth?

"We've found a way to win every game," said linebacker Fred Warner, who forced a fumble in addition to collecting 10 tackles Sunday. "And at the end of the day, the goal is just to continue to be on the rise. We're not satisfied with just winning. Of course you want to win every game.

"But the goal is to continue to get better as the season goes and I think that sets you up for the best chance to go do what you want to do at the end."

The Seahawks fell to 3-2 Sunday months after, to quote Warner, they did what teams want to do at the end.

A playoff run doesn't seem out of question for one of the league's most physical defenses and the game's best receiver. But since Darnold returned in Week 3 from a hip injury in the season opener, ball security has been a problem.

The Seahawks lost to Washington two weeks ago with three giveaways and to the 49ers on Sunday with four.

Darnold's first interception of the game came on his first throw. The Seahawks faced third-and-10, 49ers cornerback Renardo Green figured Jaxon Smith-Njigba would run to the sticks, and Green "sat on it, jumped it and made a play," he said.

On Green's second interception, which came poetically on Darnold's first throw of the second half?

"It was a double-tight end formation and one of them released," Green told reporters after the game. "He ran the over route, I played like he had a step on me. And once the ball went in the air, I just turned it on and undercut the ball.

"We didn't know how many turnovers it was going to be but we knew we was going to get our opps this game. It was on us to capitalize on every opp that we get to win."

Opportunities came also via two first-half fumbles, courtesy running back Emanuel Wilson halfway through the second quarter and running back George Holani after a punt to the 1-yard line with 13 seconds left in the first half.

For those keeping score at home, the Niners' first three touchdowns came from drives of 18 yards, 11 yards and 0 yards. Seattle's offense felt that.

"We're pissed," said Smith-Njigba, who led Seattle with 102 receiving yards and a touchdown but uncharacteristically mistimed a target on third-and-10 with the game on the line. "We wanted this one. Like I said, defense and special teams, they deserved this win. It sucks.

"As an offense, myself, I feel like we let them down. But, we're going to keep pushing."

Teammates echoed that sentiment, from Darnold saying "a lot of the guys are just pissed about not winning" to receiver Cooper Kupp confirming "without a doubt, there's frustration."

Head coach Mike Macdonald was reminded that Darnold had a stretch with eight interceptions in four games last year en route to winning the championship.

"We're not panicking … " Macdonald said. "If we become more efficient and more effective as an offense, that's going to help our quarterback, too. I think it's everybody. It's not just Sam. Sam knows.

"It's not like he wants to turn it over."

If the playoffs started this week (they don't), the 49ers would win the NFC West and NFC second seed playoff games, and the Seahawks would just miss the seventh seed to Bears and Lions teams with similar 3-2 records The Rams state their case next in Monday night's game against the Buffalo Bills .

That two of the division's teams are pacing the Rams right now diverges from league belief entering the opener.

After stockpiling edge rusher Myles Garrett, defensive tackle Aaron Donald and two veteran Chiefs cornerbacks for a defense that would complement Matthew Stafford, Puka Nacua, Davante Adams and the like?

The Rams entered this year with the best Super Bowl odds in the league. A bold scheduling decision for their opener in Australia contributed to San Francisco edging Los Angeles, 27-7. A late-game defensive pass interference that officials later said they called incorrectly contributed to the Rams' 30-26 defeat to the Denver Broncos. The Rams haven't posted a loss that gives reason to question their ability and haven't posted a win — they beat an Eagles team that lost Saquon Barkley and New York Giants team that lost Jaxson Dart — that gives credulity to their Super Bowl favoritism.

Add in injuries that have sidelined Nacua and Garrett, and there's reason to believe Los Angeles' ceiling is still in the distance.

That doesn't mean the Niners can't pace them.

"People kind of slipped on our talent all around going into this year," Warner said Sunday. "We've got guys who are ultra-talented but also could care less about what we've done in the past. We're still so eager to prove it every time we go out.

That's Mike Evans, who posted a season-best 113 yards and a score in a game where no other Niners target hit 25 yards.

There was Purdy, who finished with 189 passing yards and two touchdowns to one interception but also showed up in ways stats can't counter such as the audible to McCaffrey's touchdown run that Tom Brady outlined on the color analysis of the game.

And the 49ers' defense, in Raheem Morris' first year? Even with the injuries that seem to plague the 49ers perennially, and the second-quarter ejection of starting linebacker Dre Greenlaw , the 49ers found ways to torment Seattle's group in Seattle's house.

Oh, and Evans wasn't fazed by that vaunted house.

"My last time playing here, I think it was louder back in 2019," he said. "It's definitely loud, great environment, but I don't think it was the loudest I've been a part of."

Niners-Seahawks may not be the loudest the NFC West gets this season even after the game's bevy of takeaways and touchdowns delivered consistent entertainment.

How the Rams fare as 3.5-point home favorites against the Bills on Monday will offer the next piece of data. How the Seahawks respond from a game in which they were repeatedly in reach will, too. They'll turn around quickly to face the Broncos on Thursday night.

"I think we got a tough team," Macdonald said. "I think we're a connected team. But in terms of playing complementary football the way that we want to play here as Seahawks and become the team that we want to become?

articles.title: 3 Falcons to blame for heartbreaking Week 5 SNF loss to Ravens
articles.summary: Coach Kevin Stefanski’s Atlanta Falcons fought hard on Sunday Night Football in a game that saw backup QB Tua Tagovailoa make his debut, but came out on the...
articles.body:
Coach Kevin Stefanski 's Atlanta Falcons fought hard on Sunday Night Football in a game that saw backup QB Tua Tagovailoa make his debut , but came out on the short end of the stick in a 30-23 loss. Things started out on a positive note for Stefanski's team as Michael Penix Jr. was healthy and Jessie Bates sparked the defense with a bonkers return touchdown .

Jesse Minter's Ravens were not deterred as they fought back and tied the game up at 23-23 before overtime. Backup Ravens QB Tyler Huntley punctuated a game-winning overtime drive with a one-yard touchdown run that included a Tyler Loop extra point and set the stage for Tagovailoa's game-losing interception .

After the game, there was plenty of blame to assign as Stefanski's Falcons snatched defeat from the jaws of victory, falling to 2-3 on the season. Minter's Ravens improved their record to 4-1 on a heartbreaking, disappointing night at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, Georgia.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Here are three Falcons who deserve some heat after the rough loss to a team without its best player, starting quarterback Lamar Jackson.

Stefanski put his team in position to win throughout the night but the Falcons didn't get it done, so he will be forced to shoulder the lion's share of the blame by nature among the team's coaching staff.

Stefanski has the intelligence, experience, look and air of confidence befitting a prime time, top tier NFL coach but his record hasn't bore that out yet. He is now 47-59 in his NFL coaching career including stops at both Cleveland and Atlanta, causing fans to wonder if he will get over the hump and deliver a winning season in the ATL.

The Falcons missed out on a golden opportunity to seize control of the NFC South by surpassing the 2-2 Carolina Panthers. Instead, they fell a half-game behind Dave Canales' team and will now be forced to play catch-up in the coming weeks.

Stefanski's team once again looked crisp on offense as Penix Jr., Bijan Robinson, Drake London and others starred throughout the night, but his team was penalized seven times for 67 yards, making sloppy mistakes that simply can't happen in a prime time game of this magnitude. Many fans expected the Falcons to beat the Ravens with Lamar Jackson sidelined due to injury. Instead, they took an unfortunate and unnecessary loss that will put them behind the eight-ball for the time being.

Ulbrich's defensive unit started strong but got progressively worse throughout the contest. Huntley got support from Derrick Henry before the game and more support during the game as Henry shredded the Falcons' defense with 102 yards.

Henry also broke a nearly two-year spell with a huge play that few saw coming, including Ulbrich. Ulbrich's defense gave up 391 total yards including 5.5 yards per play to a backup quarterback. They got the huge play from Bates early but failed to turn up the heat throughout the game, squandering a raucous home field advantage and letting Huntley carve up their defense with an efficient 201 passing yards, two touchdowns and zero interceptions.

Ulbrich and the Falcons' defense has now given up 122 points on the season, second worst in the NFC South Division and among the worst defensive units in the NFC. If things don't turn around fast, Stefanski could be looking for Ulbrich's replacement this offseason.

Tagovailoa experienced dizzying highs and terrifying lows all in his first game as a Falcon. He came in with plenty of hope and completed his first pass for 14 yards before throwing the game-clinching interception in overtime with the Falcons trailing 30-23.

A little rust was to be expected from Tagovailoa as he was making his season debut after a long layoff, but he set the bar high with his first completion and then took the air out of the building with his ill-advised final throw.

Penix Jr.'s rib injury looked like it could be one that lingers going forward, putting pressure on Tagovailoa to take responsibility for his bad throw and to rally his troops after the game and into this week's practices.

"I really feel bad for Michael Penix," NFL analyst and former Jaguars star Maurice-Jones Drew said after the game , a sentiment echoed by millions of Falcons fans. Tagovailoa has the skills to be a plus starter for Stefanski's team, but his rust and sped-up mind got the best of him in Atlanta's latest loss.

Stefanski, Ulbrich, and Tagovailoa all deserve blame after the Falcons' heart-breaking setback, and getting over this loss will take a team effort with Ben Johnson's Bears coming to town on October 18.
