articles.title: Arizona Cardinals’ Points Allowed Trend Has Reached Alarming Territory
articles.summary: The Arizona Cardinals are 1-4 and aren’t getting any better. One reason is that the defense can’t stop anyone.It has been a tough first five weeks for the Ca...
articles.body:
The Arizona Cardinals are 1-4 and aren't getting any better. One reason is that the defense can't stop anyone.

It has been a tough first five weeks for the Cardinals. On Sunday, they suffered their second blowout loss at home in as many contests and traded away a former first-round pick.

Both losing big at home and moving on from former first-rounders are tough pills to swallow. But what's even more alarming? The fact that the Cardinals have allowed 31+ points per game in their last four contests and 36+ per game in their last three.

Since allowing 14 points in Week 1 against the Los Angeles Chargers, the Cardinals' defense has been one of the league's worst — though poor offensive play can account for a few of those points opponents have scored.

Arizona entered Sunday's matchup vs. the Detroit Lions with 117 points allowed, or 29.3 per game. After allowing another 45, they have now allowed 162 points, or 32.4 per game. This puts them on a 17-game pace for 551 points allowed if the trend keeps up. Per StatMuse , that would be the most points allowed in NFL history.

Arizona Cardinals Points-Allowed Trend Has Been Getting Worse

Since allowing 14 points in Week 1, the Cardinals allowed 31 points in Week 2 vs. the Seattle Seahawks . They followed that up with 36 points allowed in Weeks 3 and 4, before allowing 45 points on Sunday vs. Detroit.

Take out that stellar defensive performance in Week 1, and the Cardinals have allowed an average of 37 points per game during their losing streak. Take that number and multiply it by 16 games (taking out the 14 allowed in Week 1), and it equals 592 points allowed. That puts things into perspective about how poorly the Cardinals have played defensively — especially their passing defense .

Again, we need to place some blame on the offense's shoulders, because Jacoby Brissett and Co. have been responsible for some of those points. Most notably, Deonte Banks' pick-six in Arizona's Week 4 loss to the New York Giants .

Still, the Cardinals entered their Week 5 matchup against Detroit with the 10th-worst total defense in the NFL. They had the 12th-worst passing defense and the 13th-worst rushing defense.

The Lions Took Things Up A Notch On Sunday

The Cardinals came into Week 5 allowing a league-worst 8.0 yards per pass attempt. One of the reasons Arizona's passing defense hasn't allowed more yards is that opposing quarterbacks haven't needed to throw more than an average of 27.25 times against them.

That trend continued on Sunday , when Jared Goff completed 19-for-30 passes for 271 yards — good for 9.0 yards per pass. Throw in the 163 yards Detroit gained on the ground and 5.1 yards per carry, and it shows that the Lions spent all afternoon gashing the Cardinals' defense.

Detroit finished the game with 412 total yards, meaning the Cardinals have now allowed 1,817 yards on the season. That's 363 yards per game, and it puts the Cardinals on pace to allow 6,178 yards across 17 games.

These numbers show how far behind the Arizona Cardinals are. Right now, they don't appear to have an answer to stop the run or the pass. If there is any good news, they have 12 more games to figure this out and at least start playing respectable football.

articles.title: Jude Bellingham celebrations, Man Utd representation and the greatest NFL London game climax in history
articles.summary: NFL Sunday Review: Headbutts, brawls, ejections, Jude Bellingham celebrations and a remarkable finish to latest NFL London game asJacksonville Jaguars beat Philadelphia Eagles; watch the Jaguars against Houston Texans at Wembley Stadium, live on Sky Sports NFL from 2pm on Sunday
articles.body:
Cam Little had conjured one of the greatest moments in NFL London games history, his spine-tingling icer prompting a nod to his British stage as the Jacksonville Jaguars kicker imitated Jude Bellingham's famed celebration.

Just two weeks earlier the NFL had celebrated its Rio de Janeiro debut with a late miracle by way of Tyler Loop's game-winning field goal to lift the Baltimore Ravens past the Dallas Cowboys with one second left. On that occasion he celebrated with Cristiano Ronaldo's SIU, there having been something fitting about a kick deciding things at Brazil's Pele, Zico and Ronaldo-graced Maracana.

It was London's turn. Tottenham's turn. Jacksonville's turn. Cam Little's turn.

Little converted a 57-yard field goal with one second left to clinch a stunning 19-17 win over the Philadelphia Eagles, who had taken the lead with eight seconds left on the clock thanks to Jake Elliott's 48-yard kick.

"One of the craziest games, maybe the craziest games I've ever been a part of, and I've been in some pretty wild ones," said Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence. "Just how cool is this sport? The game's never over."

It was over. It had to be over. An Eagles-dominated Tottenham Hotspur Stadium believed it was over. A poor coaching call not to take the touchback and some Ameer Abdullah magic had other plans, the latter producing a 53-yard kick return to tee up Little's big moment.

He later joked it was the unofficial winner for his beloved Manchester United, whose shirt he wore to his post-game press conference, after they squandered Saturday's lead over Spurs. Having grown up accustomed to both codes of football, Sunday's climax would prove that little bit sweeter as he described it as the greatest moment in his career.

"A hundred per cent," said Little. "A hundred per cent. Like the record was cool and all, but it still gives me goosebumps because I don't think you guys realise I wake up every Saturday morning watching the Premier League, every Saturday, and then to play soccer from ages five to 16 - I didn't touch a football until I was almost 17. So my whole life was soccer up to that point.

"So to do it in this stadium is like I've achieved my goal of playing professional soccer even though I'm playing pro football. It's so cool. It's my first in my entire career, excluding overtime obviously, but it's the first walk off game winner I've hit in my entire career, where the clock has hit zero and we won the game."

It was a spectacle that bean in chaos and ended in chaos. Bryan Thomas Jr and Jeremiah Trotter were ejected for a brawl during a 90-yard opening kickoff return touchdown that was eventually nullified by offsetting penalties. A deafening Eagles crowd (at what was technically a Jags home game) was then the case of a false start and two delay of game penalties in the space of six plays inside the 10-yard line to prompt a seethe-fuelled ball spike from Lawrence. Parker Washington produced one of the catches of the season with a phenomenal one-handed 27-yard touchdown for a 16-14 lead, after which Littler missed the extra point.

And of course, there was the eight seconds of bedlam.

Eagles offensive tackle Jordan Mailata described it was a "week from hell", Sunday's defeat following the shock retirement of stalwart offensive tackle Lane Johnson and the trade departure of center Cam Jurgens. For Liam Coen's Jags it was dreamland for a team that has now run three in a row, this one coming in the face of a hostility rarely witnessed at an NFL London game.

One second. One kick to win it all. One Cam Little, there's only one Cam Little (if we're sticking to the football theme).

The uncomfortable conversations are coming for the Tennessee Titans and Cam Ward. That's if they haven't already started. Head coach Robert Saleh was asked about the prospect of benching his quarterback after Sunday's 26-3 loss to the Houston Texans, albeit downplaying that idea in response. But the ground is shaking beneath Ward, who isn't exactly blessed with a clear stage for success in Tennessee, while also falling short of the needle-moving influence you might expect from a No 1 pick quarterback. He finished 23 of 36 passing for 170 yards, while being sacked four times and throwing an interception. With no real threat in the running game, teams are having a field day challenging him to beat them.

Mike Evans is still doing it at an elite level at the age of 33. Brock Purdy may have never had a more reliable pair of hands at the receiver position than that of Evans since taking over at quarterback for the San Francisco 49ers a few years back. Evans had seven catches for 113 yards and a touchdown as San Francisco downed the Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks 32-29, his first 100-yard game since signing with the Niners in the offseason.

Parker Washington deserves more respect. It's not uncommon for a sixth-round wide receiver to stray from conversations centred around the elite, but whether he is or isn't part of that group, the Jaguars wideout has become indispensable for Trevor Lawrence. He had six catches for 124 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's miracle win over the Eagles, including his one-handed diving grab in the end zone to stun the Philly crowd. He is dynamic with the ball in hand, a crisp route runner and has automatic hands. You can just tell he is a dream teammate for Lawrence.

Brian Flores is currently the best non-head coach coach in the NFL. Unfortunately for the Minnesota Vikings, you suspect his days as a non-head coach are edging closer to an end, though you also wonder if he is merely enjoying the freedom of full defensive rein on his own reign of terror. Flores tormented New Orleans Saints quarterback Tyler Shough in Sunday's 23-13 win, blitzing him on 90 per cent of dropbacks in the first half and just 40 per cent in the second half while limiting him to 16 passes for 96 yards and no touchdowns. His Vikings

Jaylen Warren: Have a day, Jaylen Warren. The Steelers running back recorded 15 carries for 101 yards and a touchdown alongside a team-high six catches for 87 yards and a score as Pittsburgh beat the Indianapolis Colts 34-22 on a day that saw Aaron Rodgers throw three touchdowns in his cleanest game of the year.

Will Anderson Jr: The Texans pass rusher collected three more sacks on Sunday to continue his Defensive Player of the Year campaign as his side dominated the Tennessee Titans 26-3. He has become one of the unequivocal premier players in his position in football, and is increasingly aware of his ability to takeover games.

Ben Johnson: The Chicago Bears head coach remains one of the true geniuses in football, redefining modern offense in some ways. But when you talk as openly about your hate for an opponent, you are falling into 'loser ' territory should you fall to them. His Bears were on the wrong side of a 31-7 defeat to their fierce rival Green Bay Packers, during which Jordan Love stepped up with his most commanding performance of the season.

The Los Angeles Chargers: Jim Harbaugh's side are in turmoil. The running joke this past offseason had been the severity of their tough schedule, and as much is proving a frightening reality. They fell to 0-5 on Sunday after a 23-17 loss to the Denver Broncos, marking their worst start to a season in 23 years. What's more, Justin Herbert has thrown a second-most six interceptions and is ranked bottom in quarterback rating among qualifying players. Next up: Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs.

Player of the Weekend - Drake Maye, QB, New England Patriots

Drake Maye has shaken off his early season struggles and is beginning to look like something closer to the MVP contender that led the New England Patriots to the Super Bowl last season. He put in his most accomplished performance of the campaign on Sunday as he went 26 of 34 passing for 374 yards and four touchdowns while also rushing for 25 yards and a score in New England's 45-17 win over the Las Vegas Raiders.

Drama in London found its way to the West Coast later in the day as the San Francisco 49ers beat the Seattle Seahawks 32-29 in an epic after Eddy Pineiro's late field goal.

An action-packed game featured a season-high seven turnovers, while Brock Purdy threw two touchdowns to Evans and Brandin Cooks. 49ers linebacker Dre Greenlaw was also ejected for a head-butt on Ernest Jones, who was not wearing a helmet at the time.

Two outstanding teams and legitimate contenders going toe-to-toe, the Niners taking it to improve to 5-0 on the season as they continue their Super Bowl charge. The hearts of San Francisco fans were in their mouths when Jaxon Smith-Njigba broke free on third down late in the fourth quarter, only for the reigning Offensive Player of the Year to be guilty of a surprise drop.
